### 12.0.1 River + ocean C-PSD fits (length, surface area, volume — faceted)

Combines the per-river-location fits (Section 4.2.4) with the pooled ocean fits above into one faceted comparison, now that both are available. Rows are shape, columns are size metric; y-axis (log~10~ cumulative count) is fixed across all panels so magnitudes are directly comparable, while the x-axis (log~10~ size) is left free per metric since length/area/volume span very different numeric ranges.

```{r cpsd-river-ocean-faceted, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, echo=FALSE}
# Wrap the already-computed pooled ocean fit objects to match safe_cpsd()'s
# success-case structure (list(..., valid = TRUE)) so they drop into the same
# extract_fit_lines()/extract_fit_points() helpers used for the per-river fits.
ocean_as_location <- list(
  Ocean = list(
    length = list(
      fragment = c(cpsd_fit_ocean_frag,        list(valid = TRUE)),
      fiber    = c(cpsd_fit_ocean_fiber,        list(valid = TRUE)),
      all      = c(cpsd_fit_ocean_all,          list(valid = TRUE))
    ),
    area = list(
      fragment = c(cpsd_fit_area_ocean_frag,    list(valid = TRUE)),
      fiber    = c(cpsd_fit_area_ocean_fiber,   list(valid = TRUE)),
      all      = c(cpsd_fit_area_ocean,         list(valid = TRUE))
    ),
    volume = list(
      fragment = c(cpsd_fit_volume_ocean_frag,  list(valid = TRUE)),
      fiber    = c(cpsd_fit_volume_ocean_fiber, list(valid = TRUE)),
      all      = c(cpsd_fit_volume_ocean,       list(valid = TRUE))
    )
  )
)

cpsd_loc_shape_length_ro <- c(cpsd_loc_shape_length, list(Ocean = ocean_as_location$Ocean$length))
cpsd_loc_shape_area_ro   <- c(cpsd_loc_shape_area,   list(Ocean = ocean_as_location$Ocean$area))
cpsd_loc_shape_vol_ro    <- c(cpsd_loc_shape_vol,    list(Ocean = ocean_as_location$Ocean$volume))

locations_ro <- c(locations, "Ocean")
loc_palette_ro <- c(loc_palette, "Ocean" = "#0072B2")

cpsd_loc_lines_ro <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  extract_fit_lines(cpsd_loc_shape_length_ro, "Length (µm)"),
  extract_fit_lines(cpsd_loc_shape_area_ro,   "Surface Area (µm²)"),
  extract_fit_lines(cpsd_loc_shape_vol_ro,    "Volume (µm³)")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric   = factor(metric, levels = factor_levels$metric),
    shape    = factor(shape,  levels = factor_levels$shape, labels = factor_levels$slabel),
    location = factor(location, levels = locations_ro)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(logN_fit))

cpsd_loc_points_ro <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  extract_fit_points(cpsd_loc_shape_length_ro, "Length (µm)"),
  extract_fit_points(cpsd_loc_shape_area_ro,   "Surface Area (µm²)"),
  extract_fit_points(cpsd_loc_shape_vol_ro,    "Volume (µm³)")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric   = factor(metric, levels = factor_levels$metric),
    shape    = factor(shape,  levels = factor_levels$shape, labels = factor_levels$slabel),
    location = factor(location, levels = locations_ro)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(logN))

# Visualization-only trim (does not touch any fitted number): the fixed
# vol_bin_um bin width, applied to volume's multi-order-of-magnitude range,
# generates thousands of mostly-empty bins in the extreme long tail for any
# shape/location with even a few very-large-volume particles (their
# cumulative count N_ge stays > 0 almost to the last bin, so
# extract_fit_points()'s N_ge > 0 filter doesn't drop them) -- e.g. Carmel
# fiber's raw points span to 1.24e8 um^3 while its own fit window tops out
# near 5.8e6. With facet scales = "free_x" this stretches that one panel's
# axis so far the real fitted region (a thin sliver at the left edge)
# effectively disappears.
#
# A percentile-of-count trim does NOT fix this: bins are evenly spaced by
# vol_bin_um, so on this near-uniform grid the 99th percentile of L_low sits
# at ~99% of the full range too (barely trims the axis). Trim relative to
# each (location, shape, metric) panel's OWN fit-window upper bound instead
# (already available as max(L_low) within cpsd_loc_lines_ro's fitted line for
# that group) -- keep points out to 8x that bound, which comfortably shows
# "just outside LOD" context on every normal panel (where the full data range
# is already within a few x of the fit window) while cutting the artifact
# tail on the few panels where it runs 20x+ beyond. The underlying fit
# objects (cpsd_loc_shape_vol_ro etc.) and every computed a_cpsd/a_psd value
# are untouched -- this only changes which points are drawn.
cpsd_loc_trim_bounds <- cpsd_loc_lines_ro |>
  dplyr::group_by(location, shape, metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(lod_hi_group = max(L_low, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

cpsd_loc_points_ro <- cpsd_loc_points_ro |>
  dplyr::left_join(cpsd_loc_trim_bounds, by = c("location", "shape", "metric")) |>
  dplyr::filter(is.na(lod_hi_group) | L_low <= lod_hi_group * 8) |>
  dplyr::select(-lod_hi_group)

loc_palette_ro_used <- loc_palette_ro[names(loc_palette_ro) %in% as.character(unique(cpsd_loc_lines_ro$location))]

# Fixed y-range (shared across all facets); x stays free per facet_grid below.
y_range_ro <- range(c(cpsd_loc_lines_ro$logN_fit, cpsd_loc_points_ro$logN), na.rm = TRUE)

int_breaks <- function(x) unique(round(scales::breaks_pretty()(x)))

cpsd_river_ocean_facet_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = dplyr::filter(cpsd_loc_points_ro, !in_lod),
    ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), y = logN, color = location),
    size = 0.7, alpha = 0.05, shape = 16
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = dplyr::filter(cpsd_loc_points_ro, in_lod),
    ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), y = logN, color = location),
    size = 1.3, alpha = 0.75, shape = 16
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
    data = cpsd_loc_lines_ro,
    ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), ymin = logN_lo, ymax = logN_hi, fill = location),
    alpha = 0.12, color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = cpsd_loc_lines_ro,
    ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), y = logN_fit, color = location),
    linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    shape ~ metric,
    scales   = "free_x",
    labeller = ggplot2::label_value
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = y_range_ro) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = int_breaks, labels = function(x) round(x)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = int_breaks, labels = function(x) round(x)) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = loc_palette_ro_used, name = "River location / matrix") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual( values = loc_palette_ro_used, name = "River location / matrix") +
  ggplot2::guides(
    color = ggplot2::guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 3)),
    fill  = "none"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x        = expression(log[10] * "(size)"),
    y        = expression(log[10] * (N("">=L))),
    title    = "Power-law fits (headline fixed-window MLE): river locations + ocean, by shape and size metric",
    subtitle = "Solid lines + ribbon = fit ± 95% CI within the fit window. Faded points = outside LOD. Y-axis fixed across panels; x-axis free per metric.",
    caption  = "Rows: shape. Columns: size metric. River fits per location; ocean fit pooled. Segur (2026) LOD algorithm."
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.border    = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    strip.text      = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    plot.caption    = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50", hjust = 0)
  )

ggsave(cpsd_river_ocean_facet_plot, filename = "figures/cpsd_river_ocean_facet_plot.png",
       width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
cpsd_river_ocean_facet_plot
```

### 12.0.2 Slope comparison across matrices and metrics

Extends the per-river-location comparison (Section 4.2.5) with the pooled sediment (Section 11) and pooled ocean (Section 12.1) "all-shapes" fits for the same three size metrics, now that every matrix's area and volume fits are available. Points are colored by matrix rather than location so the four within-river points read as one group against the single pooled sediment and ocean values; the reference line previously drawn at the Segur et al. (2026) literature fragment mean is omitted here, since that value is a single-shape (fragment), single-matrix (ocean-only) literature figure and is not a like-for-like reference for a plot that already includes this study's own pooled matrix-level fits. The y-axis is fixed (not free) across the three metric facets so slope magnitudes are directly comparable panel to panel.

```{r cpsd-slopes-all-metrics-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
# Pooled ("all"-shape) sediment and ocean slopes, one row per metric, to sit
# alongside the four per-river-location rows already in loc_slopes_all
# (Section 4.2.5). Unlike river, sediment and ocean are not split by location
# here: sediment has no location field, and the ocean per-location fits
# (Section 12.0.1a) are length-only (area/volume were never fit per ocean
# location), so a single pooled point per matrix is the only like-for-like
# comparison available for all three metrics.
sed_ocean_slopes_all <- tibble::tribble(
  ~matrix,    ~metric,               ~a_cpsd,                    ~se_a_cpsd,
  "Sediment", "Length (µm)",         cpsd_fit_sed_all$a_cpsd,     cpsd_fit_sed_all$se_a_cpsd,
  "Sediment", "Surface Area (µm²)",  cpsd_fit_area_sed$a_cpsd,    cpsd_fit_area_sed$se_a_cpsd,
  "Sediment", "Volume (µm³)",        cpsd_fit_volume_sed$a_cpsd,  cpsd_fit_volume_sed$se_a_cpsd,
  "Ocean",    "Length (µm)",         cpsd_fit_ocean_all$a_cpsd,   cpsd_fit_ocean_all$se_a_cpsd,
  "Ocean",    "Surface Area (µm²)",  cpsd_fit_area_ocean$a_cpsd,  cpsd_fit_area_ocean$se_a_cpsd,
  "Ocean",    "Volume (µm³)",        cpsd_fit_volume_ocean$a_cpsd, cpsd_fit_volume_ocean$se_a_cpsd
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = matrix)

matrix_slopes_all_metrics <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(loc_slopes_all, matrix = "River", group = as.character(location)),
  sed_ocean_slopes_all
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = factor(metric, levels = c("Length (µm)", "Surface Area (µm²)", "Volume (µm³)")),
    group  = factor(group, levels = c(as.character(locations), "Sediment", "Ocean")),
    matrix = factor(matrix, levels = c("River", "Sediment", "Ocean"))
  )

matrix_pal_slopes <- c("River" = "#0072B2", "Sediment" = "#E69F00", "Ocean" = "#009E73")

cpsd_slopes_all_metrics_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(matrix_slopes_all_metrics,
    ggplot2::aes(x = group, y = a_cpsd, color = matrix)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 4) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
    ggplot2::aes(ymin = a_cpsd - se_a_cpsd, ymax = a_cpsd + se_a_cpsd),
    width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ metric, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = matrix_pal_slopes, name = "Matrix") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x        = "Location (river) / matrix (sediment, ocean)",
    y        = expression(italic(a)[cpsd]),
    title    = "Headline slope (as a_cpsd = a_psd + 1) by location/matrix and size metric",
    subtitle = "Error bars = ±1 SE. River shown per location; sediment and ocean are pooled matrix-level fits."
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 20) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    strip.text   = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave(cpsd_slopes_all_metrics_plot, filename = "figures/cpsd_slopes_all_metrics_plot.png", width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
cpsd_slopes_all_metrics_plot
```

## 12.1.1 All-matrix particle-length PSD comparison with MPSizeBase

This section is intentionally placed after the river, sediment, and ocean length C-PSDs have all been calculated. It imports the MPSizeBase workbook v19-5-2026 (Zenodo, DOI [10.5281/zenodo.20832480](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20832480), record v5, CC BY 4.0; file `data_input/MPsizeBase v19-5-2026.xlsx`, MD5 bd31cb5863cf1022f3717d219e2e6865, asserted below), reads the workbook `Read Me`, and parses one literature *a*~psd~ value per `PSD_ID` from the `Literature PSD data` tab. The `cumsum_powerlaw_alpha` column is already the converted BN-PSD/differential slope (*a*~psd~ = *a*~cpsd~ - 1), so no additional conversion is applied. This study's rows show the headline slopes (maximum likelihood on a fixed 100–500 µm window). The MPsizeBase values are C-PSD fits, so the like-for-like comparison against our C-PSD fits is given in Section 13.6 (D4).

```{r alpha-comparison-all-matrices-mpsizebase, fig.width=12, fig.height=7, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
mpsizebase_path <- file.path(proj_root, "data_input", "MPsizeBase v19-5-2026.xlsx")
mpsizebase_md5 <- "bd31cb5863cf1022f3717d219e2e6865"  # Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20832480 (v5)
stopifnot("MPsizeBase workbook checksum mismatch" = unname(tools::md5sum(mpsizebase_path)) == mpsizebase_md5)

mpsizebase_readme <- readxl::read_excel(
  mpsizebase_path,
  sheet = "Read Me",
  col_names = FALSE
) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_any(dplyr::everything(), ~ !is.na(.x)))

knitr::kable(
  mpsizebase_readme,
  caption = "MPSizeBase workbook Read Me sheet"
)

mpsizebase_literature_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  mpsizebase_path,
  sheet = "Literature PSD data",
  skip = 2,
  .name_repair = "unique"
)

required_mpsizebase_cols <- c(
  "PSD_ID", "Study", "Year", "Ocean", "Sample_type", "MP_shape",
  "Low_size", "High_size", "cumsum_slope", "cumsum_powerlaw_alpha"
)
missing_mpsizebase_cols <- setdiff(required_mpsizebase_cols, names(mpsizebase_literature_raw))
if (length(missing_mpsizebase_cols) > 0) {
  stop("MPSizeBase Literature PSD data sheet is missing columns: ",
       paste(missing_mpsizebase_cols, collapse = ", "))
}

literature_psd_alpha <- mpsizebase_literature_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(PSD_ID), !is.na(cumsum_powerlaw_alpha)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(PSD_ID) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Study = dplyr::first(Study),
    Year = dplyr::first(Year),
    Literature_matrix = dplyr::first(Sample_type),
    Ocean_or_region = dplyr::first(Ocean),
    Shape = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("fiber", dplyr::first(MP_shape), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "fiber",
      grepl("fragment", dplyr::first(MP_shape), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "fragment",
      TRUE ~ as.character(dplyr::first(MP_shape))
    ),
    n_bins = dplyr::n(),
    a_cpsd = dplyr::first(as.numeric(cumsum_slope)),
    a_psd = dplyr::first(as.numeric(cumsum_powerlaw_alpha)),
    # Fitted LOD window = the filtered (fit) bins, not the full reported bin range.
    lod_low_um = suppressWarnings(min(as.numeric(filtered_low_size), na.rm = TRUE)),
    lod_high_um = suppressWarnings(max(as.numeric(filtered_high_size), na.rm = TRUE)),
    bins_low_um = suppressWarnings(min(as.numeric(Low_size), na.rm = TRUE)),
    bins_high_um = suppressWarnings(max(as.numeric(High_size), na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Source = "Segur et al. MPSizeBase",
    Matrix = dplyr::case_when(
      Literature_matrix == "Ocean" ~ "Literature ocean",
      Literature_matrix == "Atmosphere" ~ "Literature atmosphere",
      TRUE ~ paste("Literature", Literature_matrix)
    ),
    alpha_abs = abs(a_psd),
    label = PSD_ID
  )

fit_to_alpha_row <- function(matrix_label, shape_label, fit, psd_id, source_detail) {
  tibble::tibble(
    PSD_ID = psd_id,
    Study = "This study",
    Year = NA_real_,
    Source = source_detail,
    Matrix = matrix_label,
    Shape = shape_label,
    n_bins = fit$n_bins,
    n_window = fit$n_window %||% NA_real_,
    a_cpsd = fit$a_cpsd,
    a_psd = fit$a_psd,
    se_a_psd = fit$se_a_psd,
    lod_low_um = fit$lower_lod_used_um,
    lod_high_um = fit$upper_lod_um,
    alpha_abs = abs(fit$a_psd),
    label = psd_id
  )
}

this_study_length_alpha <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fit_to_alpha_row("River water", "all", cpsd_fit_all, "W2W_river_all", "This study matrix/shape"),
  fit_to_alpha_row("River water", "fragment", cpsd_fit_frag, "W2W_river_fragment", "This study matrix/shape"),
  fit_to_alpha_row("River water", "fiber", cpsd_fit_fiber, "W2W_river_fiber", "This study matrix/shape"),
  fit_to_alpha_row("Sediment", "all", cpsd_fit_sed_all, "W2W_sediment_all", "This study matrix/shape"),
  fit_to_alpha_row("Sediment", "fragment", cpsd_fit_sed_frag, "W2W_sediment_fragment", "This study matrix/shape"),
  fit_to_alpha_row("Sediment", "fiber", cpsd_fit_sed_fiber, "W2W_sediment_fiber", "This study matrix/shape"),
  fit_to_alpha_row("Ocean water", "all", cpsd_fit_ocean_all, "W2W_ocean_all", "This study matrix/shape"),
  fit_to_alpha_row("Ocean water", "fragment", cpsd_fit_ocean_frag, "W2W_ocean_fragment", "This study matrix/shape"),
  fit_to_alpha_row("Ocean water", "fiber", cpsd_fit_ocean_fiber, "W2W_ocean_fiber", "This study matrix/shape"),
  loc_summary |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      PSD_ID = paste0("W2W_river_site_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", location)),
      Study = "This study",
      Year = NA_real_,
      Source = "This study river site",
      Matrix = "River water",
      Shape = "all-site",
      n_bins = n_bins,
      a_cpsd = a_cpsd,
      a_psd = a_psd,
      lod_low_um = lod_low_um,
      lod_high_um = lod_high_um,
      alpha_abs = abs(a_psd),
      label = location
    )
)

## Freshwater/marine-only comparison, extended with Wang/Zhao/Kooi literature
##
## Per revision: literature "atmosphere" values are dropped (not a useful
## comparator for aquatic matrices), as is the sediment matrix (neither
## freshwater nor marine surface water). This study is split into its own
## River (freshwater) and Ocean (marine) rows, each retaining the
## fragment/fiber/all shape distinction and this-study point labels. Three
## additional literature sources reported in Section 4.2.1.2 are added:
## Wang et al. (2026), Segur et al. (2026) ocean reference, and Kooi et al.
## (2021) freshwater/marine defaults, plus Zhao et al. (2026). Zhao's
## meta-analysis only reports a pooled mean +/- SD across 45 studies (no
## per-study values, no fragment/fiber split, and the underlying studies mix
## freshwater and marine sites) -- it is therefore plotted as a single
## point +/- SD, shape "all", in an "unclassified" matrix color rather than
## forced into freshwater or marine.

literature_ocean_only <- literature_psd_alpha |>
  dplyr::filter(Matrix == "Literature ocean")

dropped_literature_matrix <- literature_psd_alpha |>
  dplyr::filter(Matrix != "Literature ocean") |>
  dplyr::count(Matrix, name = "n_PSD_IDs")
if (nrow(dropped_literature_matrix) > 0) {
  cat("MPSizeBase literature PSD_IDs excluded from the freshwater/marine comparison ",
      "(not ocean, e.g. atmosphere):\n", sep = "")
  print(dropped_literature_matrix)
}

# Deterministic within-row x offsets (added at source, not recomputed from a
# shared group size later) so fragment/fiber/all never collide with the
# per-site cluster regardless of how many river sites there are.
shape_offset <- function(shape) dplyr::case_when(
  shape == "fragment" ~ -0.15,
  shape == "fiber"    ~  0.15,
  TRUE                ~  0
)

this_study_river_shape <- this_study_length_alpha |>
  dplyr::filter(Matrix == "River water") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Source = "This study — River (freshwater)",
    Matrix = "Freshwater",
    Shape,
    alpha_abs,
    se = se_a_psd,
    se_kind = "SE",
    point_label = Shape,
    n_desc = paste0("n = ", n_window, " particles in the fit window (MLE)"),
    lod_desc = paste0(round(lod_low_um), "–", round(lod_high_um), " µm (fixed MLE window)"),
    offset = shape_offset(Shape)
  )

this_study_ocean_shape <- this_study_length_alpha |>
  dplyr::filter(Matrix == "Ocean water") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Source = "This study — Ocean (marine)",
    Matrix = "Marine",
    Shape,
    alpha_abs,
    se = se_a_psd,
    se_kind = "SE",
    point_label = Shape,
    n_desc = paste0("n = ", n_window, " particles in the fit window (MLE)"),
    lod_desc = paste0(round(lod_low_um), "–", round(lod_high_um), " µm (fixed MLE window)"),
    offset = shape_offset(Shape)
  )

# Per-site points sit in their own band (0.30-0.30+0.02*(n-1)) above the
# fragment/fiber/all cluster (-0.15 to 0.15), so they never overlap it.
this_study_river_sites <- loc_summary |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Source = "This study — River (freshwater)",
    Matrix = "Freshwater",
    Shape = "all-site",
    alpha_abs = abs(a_psd),
    se = se_a_cpsd,
    se_kind = "SE",
    point_label = location,
    n_desc = paste0("n = ", n_window, " particles in the fit window (MLE)"),
    lod_desc = paste0(round(lod_low_um), "–", round(lod_high_um), " µm (fixed MLE window)"),
    offset = 0.30 + 0.02 * (dplyr::row_number() - 1)
  )

# Wang et al. (2026): actual per-site fits (Talanta 296, 128417, sec. 3.1.2).
# Combined n = 6 samples (2 Eijsden + 4 Lobith); Lobith n = 4; Eijsden n = 2.
# SD values are the reported fit SDs, used here as the plotted error bar.
wang_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Source      = "Wang et al. 2026 — Rhine/Meuse rivers (freshwater, µFTIR)",
  Matrix      = "Freshwater",
  Shape       = "all",
  alpha_abs   = c(3.65, 3.89, 3.19),
  se          = c(0.21, 0.36, 0.58),
  se_kind     = "SD",
  point_label = c("Combined", "Lobith (Rhine)", "Eijsden (Meuse)"),
  n_desc      = c("n = 6 samples (pooled fit)", "n = 4 samples (site mean)", "n = 2 samples (site mean)"),
  lod_desc    = c("118 µm (min, pooled fit)", "38–92 µm (per-sample range)", "35–90 µm (per-sample range)"),
  offset      = c(-0.2, 0, 0.2)
)

segur_ocean_ref_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Source      = "Segur et al. 2026 — ocean reference (marine, C-PSD)",
  Matrix      = "Marine",
  Shape       = "all",
  alpha_abs   = 2.66,
  se          = NA_real_,
  se_kind     = NA_character_,
  point_label = NA_character_,
  n_desc      = "Reference default (not sample-based)",
  lod_desc    = "Not reported",
  offset      = 0
)

kooi_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Source      = c("Kooi et al. 2021 — freshwater default", "Kooi et al. 2021 — marine default"),
  Matrix      = c("Freshwater", "Marine"),
  Shape       = "all",
  alpha_abs   = c(kooi_alpha_freshwater, kooi_alpha_marine),
  se          = c(PSSDplusplus::param_default_values$alpha.freshwater.sd,
                   PSSDplusplus::param_default_values$alpha.marine.sd),
  se_kind     = "SE",
  point_label = NA_character_,
  n_desc      = "PSSDplusplus::param_default_values literature synthesis default",
  lod_desc    = "Not reported",
  offset      = 0
)

# Zhao et al. (2026): only a pooled mean +/- SD across 45 studies is reported
# (Fig. 4a); no per-study values, no fragment/fiber split, freshwater/marine
# not separated in source. Plotted as point + SD (not a boxplot) per Zhao's
# own reporting, with an unclassified "mixed" matrix color.
zhao_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Source      = "Zhao et al. 2026 — global surface water (mixed F+M, unclassified)",
  Matrix      = "Mixed (unclassified)",
  Shape       = "all",
  alpha_abs   = c(1.50, 1.53),
  se          = c(0.53, NA_real_),
  se_kind     = "SD",
  point_label = c("Raw (unadjusted)", "Mesh-adjusted"),
  n_desc      = "n = 45 studies (meta-analysis; freshwater + marine pooled, not separated in source)",
  lod_desc    = "10–5000 µm (model domain)",
  offset      = c(-0.15, 0.15)
)

literature_ocean_df <- literature_ocean_only |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    # Segur et al. fit fragments and fibers separately: keep them as separate rows.
    Source      = paste0("Literature ocean (MPSizeBase compilation, marine) — ", Shape, "s"),
    Matrix      = "Marine",
    Shape       = Shape,
    alpha_abs,
    se          = NA_real_,
    se_kind     = NA_character_,
    point_label = NA_character_,
    n_desc      = paste0("PSD_ID = ", PSD_ID),
    lod_desc    = paste0(round(lod_low_um), "–", round(lod_high_um), " µm"),
    offset      = 0
  )

source_levels_bottom_to_top <- c(
  "Zhao et al. 2026 — global surface water (mixed F+M, unclassified)",
  "Kooi et al. 2021 — marine default",
  "Segur et al. 2026 — ocean reference (marine, C-PSD)",
  "Literature ocean (MPSizeBase compilation, marine) — fibers",
  "Literature ocean (MPSizeBase compilation, marine) — fragments",
  "This study — Ocean (marine)",
  "Kooi et al. 2021 — freshwater default",
  "Wang et al. 2026 — Rhine/Meuse rivers (freshwater, µFTIR)",
  "This study — River (freshwater)"
)

# Y-axis labels (post coord_flip): "Study - Location" only -- Matrix is
# already encoded by point/box color, so it's dropped from the parenthetical
# here; N is appended where one representative sample size applies to the
# whole row (rows with multiple different per-point N's, e.g. "This study",
# are left without one and rely on the per-point metadata table below instead).
source_labels_clean <- c(
  "Zhao et al. 2026 — global surface water (mixed F+M, unclassified)" = "Zhao et al. 2026 - Global surface water (N=45 studies)",
  "Kooi et al. 2021 — marine default"                                 = "Kooi et al. 2021 - Marine default",
  "Segur et al. 2026 — ocean reference (marine, C-PSD)"               = "Segur et al. 2026 - Ocean reference",
  "Literature ocean (MPSizeBase compilation, marine) — fragments"     = paste0("Literature ocean fragments (MPSizeBase) (N=", sum(literature_ocean_only$Shape == "fragment"), ")"),
  "Literature ocean (MPSizeBase compilation, marine) — fibers"        = paste0("Literature ocean fibers (MPSizeBase) (N=", sum(literature_ocean_only$Shape == "fiber"), ")"),
  "This study — Ocean (marine)"                                       = "This study - Ocean",
  "Kooi et al. 2021 — freshwater default"                             = "Kooi et al. 2021 - Freshwater default",
  "Wang et al. 2026 — Rhine/Meuse rivers (freshwater, µFTIR)"         = "Wang et al. 2026 - Rhine/Meuse rivers (N=6 samples)",
  "This study — River (freshwater)"                                   = "This study - River"
)

alpha_forest_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  this_study_river_shape, this_study_river_sites, this_study_ocean_shape,
  wang_df, segur_ocean_ref_df, kooi_df, literature_ocean_df, zhao_df
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Source     = factor(Source, levels = source_levels_bottom_to_top),
    Matrix     = factor(Matrix, levels = c("Freshwater", "Marine", "Mixed (unclassified)")),
    Shape      = factor(Shape, levels = c("fragment", "fiber", "all", "all-site")),
    is_this_study   = grepl("^This study", Source),
    is_boxplot_row  = grepl("^Literature ocean", Source),
    # offset was fixed at each source-piece's own construction (above), so it
    # is never recomputed from a mismatched/shared group size here.
    x_pos = as.numeric(Source) + offset,
    # ci_mult: 1.96 for genuine standard-error sources (a true 95% CI, normal
    # approximation) -- Kooi et al. and This Study (se_a_psd/se_a_cpsd from
    # the C-PSD fits). 1 for sources whose "se" column is actually a reported
    # SD (Wang, Zhao -- both explicitly documented as SD in this plot's
    # caption already), left as +-1 SD rather than mislabeled as a CI.
    ci_mult = dplyr::if_else(se_kind == "SE", 1.96, 1)
  )

matrix_pal_forest <- c(
  "Freshwater"            = "#0072B2",
  "Marine"                = "#009E73",
  "Mixed (unclassified)"  = "#999999"
)
shape_pal_forest <- c(fragment = 16, fiber = 17, all = 15, "all-site" = 1)


alpha_comparison_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  alpha_forest_df,
  ggplot2::aes(x = x_pos, y = alpha_abs)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    data = alpha_forest_df |> dplyr::filter(is_boxplot_row),
    ggplot2::aes(group = Source, fill = Matrix),
    color = "#009E73", alpha = 0.12, width = 0.55, outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
    # 95% CI (+-1.96 x SE, normal approximation) for genuine-SE sources:
    # Kooi et al. (param_default_values .sd fields) and This Study
    # (se_a_psd/se_a_cpsd from the C-PSD fits, wired in above; was previously
    # hardcoded NA here). Wang/Zhao's bars stay +-1 SD (ci_mult = 1), matching
    # what this plot's own caption already documents them as. Segur et al.'s
    # single ocean reference value has no SE to show (a fixed literature
    # default, not a fitted estimate with its own uncertainty) -- correctly
    # stays without a bar.
    data = alpha_forest_df |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(se)),
    ggplot2::aes(ymin = alpha_abs - ci_mult * se, ymax = alpha_abs + ci_mult * se, color = Matrix),
    width = 0.10, linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    data = alpha_forest_df |> dplyr::filter(is_boxplot_row),
    ggplot2::aes(color = Matrix, shape = Shape),
    width = 0.24, height = 0, alpha = 0.35, size = 1.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = alpha_forest_df |> dplyr::filter(!is_boxplot_row),
    ggplot2::aes(color = Matrix, shape = Shape),
    size = 3.2, alpha = 0.95
  ) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = alpha_forest_df |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(point_label)),
    ggplot2::aes(label = point_label),
    size = 3.0, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE,
    box.padding = 0.4, point.padding = 0.2, force = 2, force_pull = 0.5,
    min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = 0.3, segment.alpha = 0.5, seed = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = matrix_pal_forest, drop = FALSE, name = "Matrix") +

      sep = "\n"
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "Colors match freshwater/marine usage elsewhere in this document (blue = freshwater, green = marine). ",

      "Wang et al. and Zhao et al. show +-1 reported SD (not a CI -- see below); Segur et al.'s ocean reference is a ",
      "fixed literature default with no fitted uncertainty, so it has no error bar. ",
      "Zhao et al. (2026) is unclassified gray because its 45-study meta-analysis pools freshwater and marine sites ",
      "and reports only a pooled mean ± SD (no per-study values or shape split), plotted as point ± SD rather than a boxplot. ",
      "Literature ocean (MPSizeBase) box+jitter uses ", nrow(literature_ocean_only), " individual PSD_IDs. ",
      "Wang et al. (2026) SDs are the reported per-fit SDs (Talanta 296, 128417)."
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray82", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10.5, color = "gray30"),
```

## 12.3 Marine toxicity data

```{r ocean-tox-data}
tox_data_ocean <- tomex2 |>
  dplyr::filter(
    env_f            == "Marine",
    Group            != "Bacterium",
    Group            != "Plant",
    effect.metric    != "HONEC",
    tier_zero_tech_f == "Red Criteria Passed",
    tier_zero_risk_f == "Red Criteria Passed",
    risk.13          != 0
  )

cat("Marine tox endpoints:", nrow(tox_data_ocean), "records,",
    length(unique(tox_data_ocean$Group)), "taxonomic groups\n")
```

### Parameter distributions

```{r ocean-aspect-ratio}
set.seed(9003)
R.ave_ocean_result <- bootstrap_aspect_ratio(raw_particles_ocean$aspect_ratio, n_boot = n_boot)
R.ave_ocean_vals   <- R.ave_ocean_result$vals
R.ave_ocean_mean   <- R.ave_ocean_result$boot_mean
R.ave_ocean_sd     <- R.ave_ocean_result$boot_sd

param_values_ocean <- PSSDplusplus::param_default_values

param_values_ocean[["alpha.marine"]]          <- -alpha_ocean_mu
param_values_ocean[["alpha.marine.sd"]]       <- alpha_ocean_se
param_values_ocean[["R.ave.water.marine"]]    <- R.ave_ocean_mean
param_values_ocean[["R.ave.water.marine.sd"]] <- R.ave_ocean_sd
# use the differential a_psd = a_cpsd - 1, not the cumulative a_cpsd
# (the cumulative value is 1.0 too shallow; see river/sediment blocks above).
param_values_ocean[["a.sa.marine"]]           <- -cpsd_fit_area_ocean$a_psd
param_values_ocean[["a.sa.marine.sd"]]        <- cpsd_fit_area_ocean$se_a_psd
param_values_ocean[["a.v.marine"]]            <- -cpsd_fit_volume_ocean$a_psd
param_values_ocean[["a.v.marine.sd"]]         <- cpsd_fit_volume_ocean$se_a_psd
# a.m.marine: use volume slope as proxy (mass ∝ density × volume; constant density → same slope)
param_values_ocean[["a.m.marine"]]            <- -cpsd_fit_volume_ocean$a_psd
param_values_ocean[["a.m.marine.sd"]]         <- cpsd_fit_volume_ocean$se_a_psd
# Keep all remaining params from param_default_values (same pattern as river section)
# a.ssa.marine, p.ave.marine etc. retain their validated defaults
param_values_ocean

# SPEC 1b acceptance check: a.v and a.m must be mutually consistent
stopifnot(abs(param_values_ocean$a.v.marine - param_values_ocean$a.m.marine) < 0.3)
```

## Results at a glance

```{r results-box-inline, include=FALSE}
rb_river_fd <- dplyr::filter(mc2d_summary, ERM == "Food Dilution",        HCx == 5)
rb_river_tt <- dplyr::filter(mc2d_summary, ERM == "Tissue Translocation", HCx == 5)
rb_sed_fd   <- dplyr::filter(risk_summary_sed, ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5)
```

> **River and ocean water (the quantitative headline result).** At HC5, river water Food Dilution median RQ = `r round(rb_river_fd$RQ_p50_med, 2)` (P(RQ>1) = `r round(rb_river_fd$P_exceed_med*100,1)`%) and Tissue Translocation median RQ = `r round(rb_river_tt$RQ_p50_med, 3)` (P(RQ>1) = `r round(rb_river_tt$P_exceed_med*100,1)`%); ocean water Food Dilution median RQ = `r round(rs_ocean_food_hc5$RQ_p50_med, 2)` (P(RQ>1) = `r round(rs_ocean_food_hc5$P_exceed_med*100,1)`%) and Tissue Translocation median RQ = `r round(rs_ocean_tissue_hc5$RQ_p50_med, 3)` (P(RQ>1) = `r round(rs_ocean_tissue_hc5$P_exceed_med*100,1)`%). **A food-dilution threshold exceedance cannot be excluded, but it is method-conditional** (floor-sensitive and driven by which toxicity studies enter the food-dilution SSD, not by exposure extrapolation alone -- Section 12.5.1.3.1); **Tissue Translocation is below threshold at the median for both matrices.** The single-slope exposure correction (used above), a piecewise (dual-slope) bounding sensitivity, and an MLE/lognormal extrapolation-model comparison (Section 12.5.2) together bracket the sub-detection-limit extrapolation; all are quantified in the Sensitivity & structural uncertainty section below. **Sediment is excluded from this conclusion**: its exposure concentration is a per-liter water value with no dry-mass basis, not a genuine particles/kg-dry-weight measurement, and its nominal Food Dilution RQ (`r formatC(round(rb_sed_fd$RQ_p50), format = "d", big.mark = ",")`, P = `r round(rb_sed_fd$P_exceed*100)`%) fails a benthic-plausibility guard by roughly eleven orders of magnitude (Section 11). A fully quantified executive summary, including the RQ decomposition that separates the exposure/length-slope/area-slope/volume-slope contributions, follows in Key Findings below.

---

```{r spec1b-legacy-ocean-pipeline, include=FALSE, cache=TRUE, cache.extra=list(n_boot, raw_data_cache_key)}
  param_matrix = param_matrix_legacy_ocean,
  environments = c("Marine"),
  cache_suffix = "ocean_legacy_av",
  dose_unit    = "L",
  n_sim        = n_boot,
  num_cores    = parallel::detectCores() - 2,
  sim          = 30,
  cv_uf        = 0.5,
  rmore_method = "lognormal",
  seed         = 5006
)
haz_legacy_ocean         <- build_haz_df(ocean_pssd_legacy$pSSDs, "Marine")
rm(ocean_pssd_legacy); invisible(gc())   # several GB at production budgets; only the hazard table is used
set.seed(9306)
risk_draws_legacy_ocean  <- draw_rq_mc1d(haz_legacy_ocean, eed_boot_ocean$q50, n_risk = n_risk_ocean)
risk_summary_legacy_ocean <- summarize_rq(risk_draws_legacy_ocean)
```

Hoffman et al. (2026) frame the observed PSD as a transport-filtered distribution. A simple diagnostic is the capture fraction *f*(*d*, δ) = 1 − exp(−*w*~s~(*d*)·δ / *K*) and the critical size where *w*~s~(*d*)·δ / *K* ≈ 1. The calculation below uses Stokes settling/rise speed with user-supplied `delta_m` = `r hoffman_delta_m` m and `K_m2_s` = `r hoffman_K_m2_s` m^2/s. These are assumptions, not measured site parameters, and should be replaced with field-specific values before a mechanistic transport correction is attempted.

```{r hoffman-critical-size-piecewise}
matrix_fit_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Matrix = c("River water", "Sediment", "Ocean water"),
  cpsd_fit = list(cpsd_fit_all, cpsd_fit_sed_all, cpsd_fit_ocean_all),
  median_density_g_cm3 = c(
    median(raw_particles_river$density_g_cm3, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(raw_particles_sed$density_g_cm3, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(raw_particles_ocean$density_g_cm3, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  water_density_g_cm3 = c(1.00, 1.00, 1.025)
)

critical_piecewise_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(matrix_fit_tbl)), function(i) {
  fit_i <- matrix_fit_tbl$cpsd_fit[[i]]
  dc_i <- estimate_critical_size(
    delta_m = hoffman_delta_m,
    K_m2_s = hoffman_K_m2_s,
    density_g_cm3 = matrix_fit_tbl$median_density_g_cm3[i],
    water_density_g_cm3 = matrix_fit_tbl$water_density_g_cm3[i]
  )
  pw_i <- piecewise_cpsd_diagnostic(fit_i)
  tibble::tibble(
    Matrix = matrix_fit_tbl$Matrix[i],
    median_density_g_cm3 = matrix_fit_tbl$median_density_g_cm3[i],
    critical_size_um = dc_i,
    fit_lod_low_um = fit_i$lower_lod_used_um,
    fit_lod_high_um = fit_i$upper_lod_um,
    straddles_critical_size = is.finite(dc_i) && dc_i >= fit_i$lower_lod_used_um && dc_i <= fit_i$upper_lod_um,
    single_a_cpsd = fit_i$a_cpsd,
    single_a_psd = fit_i$a_psd,
    piecewise_break_um = pw_i$break_um,
    piecewise_low_a_cpsd = pw_i$slope_low,
    piecewise_high_a_cpsd = pw_i$slope_high,
    piecewise_delta_aic = pw_i$delta_aic
  )
}))

knitr::kable(
  critical_piecewise_tbl,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "SPEC 4 diagnostic: critical size and two-segment C-PSD fit by matrix"
)
```

The piecewise fits are diagnostic only. A fit window that straddles the assumed critical size is flagged because the fitted single slope may blend a transport-distorted fine-size regime with the coarser-size regime. Per Hoffman et al. (2026), future refinement should prioritize measured 3-D geometry and polymer density over increasingly elaborate settling equations; even precise-geometry settling models retain substantial residual error, so settling-based corrections should be treated as bias-level adjustments rather than high-precision concentration estimates.

### 13.2.1 Single-slope vs. two-segment fits with binned data (particle length only)

Visualizes the two competing exposure-side models directly against the binned C-PSD data, using the same visual grammar as `plot_cpsd_multi()` (Section 4.2.1.1/Figure `river_length_cpsd_plot`): points outside the fitted LOD window shown at reduced opacity, dotted vertical lines marking the LOD window boundaries, and a 95% CI ribbon around each regression line. Restricted to particle length (the metric the piecewise bounding sensitivity, Section 13.3, actually uses); the analogous area/volume comparison is not produced, since the piecewise model is not fit for those metrics. Colors distinguish matrix (river/sediment/ocean); the two-segment panel's break point for each matrix (Section 13.2 table above) is visible directly as the bend in that matrix's line rather than marked separately, since the gap between the two fitted panels already makes the two-segment shape distinguishable from the single-slope one.

```{r cpsd-single-vs-piecewise-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
# Reuses the already-computed pooled "all"-shape length fits (no new fitting):
# cpsd_fit_all / cpsd_fit_sed_all / cpsd_fit_ocean_all for the single-slope
# model, and critical_piecewise_tbl$piecewise_break_um (this section, above)
# for where to split each matrix's two-segment model. The two-segment lines
# are obtained by refitting a plain lm(log10(N_ge) ~ log10(L_low)) separately
# on each side of the break, over the *same* LOD-window bins already selected
# by the single-slope fit (fo$data) -- i.e. an unconstrained-intercept version
# of the same segment-interaction model piecewise_cpsd_diagnostic() already
# fit to choose that break point, just refit here to recover per-segment
# intercepts for plotting (the diagnostic function only returns slopes/AIC).
cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix <- list(
  "River water" = cpsd_fit_all,
  "Sediment"    = cpsd_fit_sed_all,
  "Ocean water" = cpsd_fit_ocean_all
)
# Points/legend use the standard (medium-saturation) matrix palette; regression
# lines use a separately darkened variant of the same hues so the fit lines
# read clearly against the dense point cloud rather than blending into it.
matrix_pal_cpsd      <- c("River water" = "#0072B2", "Sediment" = "#E69F00", "Ocean water" = "#009E73")
matrix_pal_cpsd_dark <- c("River water" = "#00375C", "Sediment" = "#7A5300", "Ocean water" = "#00432F")

df_all_ms <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix), function(mat) {
  fo <- cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix[[mat]]
  fo$bins |>
    dplyr::arrange(L_low) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      N_ge   = rev(cumsum(rev(n))),
      Matrix = mat,
      in_lod = L_low >= fo$lower_lod_used_um & L_high <= fo$upper_lod_um
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(L_low > 0, N_ge > 0, n > 0)
}))

pred_single_ms <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix), function(mat) {
  fo <- cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix[[mat]]   # headline fit (fixed-window MLE) -- drawn with fit_curve_logN()
  dplyr::mutate(fit_curve_logN(fo, seq(fo$lower_lod_used_um, fo$upper_lod_um, length.out = 200)), Matrix = mat, .before = 1)
}))

pred_piecewise_ms <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix), function(mat) {
  fo  <- cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix[[mat]]
  brk <- critical_piecewise_tbl$piecewise_break_um[critical_piecewise_tbl$Matrix == mat]
  if (!is.finite(brk)) return(NULL)
  dat <- dplyr::mutate(fo$data, log_L = log10(L_low), log_N = log10(N_ge))
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("low", "high"), function(seg) {
    sub <- if (seg == "low") dplyr::filter(dat, L_low < brk) else dplyr::filter(dat, L_low >= brk)
    if (nrow(sub) < 2) return(NULL)
    fit_seg <- stats::lm(log_N ~ log_L, data = sub)
    grid    <- tibble::tibble(L_low = seq(min(sub$L_low), max(sub$L_low), length.out = 100))
    p       <- predict(fit_seg, newdata = data.frame(log_L = log10(grid$L_low)), se.fit = TRUE)
    tibble::tibble(Matrix = mat, segment = seg, L_low = grid$L_low, logN_fit = p$fit,
                   logN_lo = p$fit - 1.96 * p$se.fit, logN_hi = p$fit + 1.96 * p$se.fit)
  }))
}))

lod_bounds_ms <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix), function(mat) {
  fo <- cpsd_length_fits_by_matrix[[mat]]
  tibble::tibble(Matrix = mat, xval = log10(c(fo$lower_lod_used_um, fo$upper_lod_um)))
}))

model_levels <- c("Single-slope (production)", "Two-segment (piecewise)")

df_both_ms <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(df_all_ms, Model = model_levels[1]),
  dplyr::mutate(df_all_ms, Model = model_levels[2])
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = model_levels))

pred_single_ms    <- dplyr::mutate(pred_single_ms,    Model = factor(model_levels[1], levels = model_levels),
                                    line_color = unname(matrix_pal_cpsd_dark[Matrix]))
pred_piecewise_ms <- dplyr::mutate(pred_piecewise_ms, Model = factor(model_levels[2], levels = model_levels),
                                    line_color = unname(matrix_pal_cpsd_dark[Matrix]))

lod_bounds_both_ms <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(lod_bounds_ms, Model = model_levels[1]),
  dplyr::mutate(lod_bounds_ms, Model = model_levels[2])
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = model_levels))

# Layer order matters: points are drawn first, then a dark "halo" line
# (thicker, neutral grey, semi-transparent) beneath the actual colored fit
# line, so the fit line reads clearly on top of the point cloud regardless of
# how dense the points are. The fit lines themselves use matrix_pal_cpsd_dark
# via aes(color = I(line_color)) -- a literal (AsIs) color that bypasses the
# shared discrete color scale, so lines can be darker than points without a
# second/conflicting legend.
cpsd_single_vs_piecewise_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(df_both_ms, ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), y = log10(N_ge), color = Matrix)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    data = lod_bounds_both_ms, ggplot2::aes(xintercept = xval),
    linetype = "dotted", color = "gray55", linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(alpha = in_lod), size = 1.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
    data = pred_single_ms, ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), ymin = logN_lo, ymax = logN_hi, fill = Matrix),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.15, color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
    data = pred_piecewise_ms,
    ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), ymin = logN_lo, ymax = logN_hi, fill = Matrix, group = interaction(Matrix, segment)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.15, color = NA
  ) +
  # Dark halo behind the single-slope line (contrast against the point cloud).
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = pred_single_ms, ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), y = logN_fit, group = Matrix),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey15", alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 2.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = pred_single_ms, ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), y = logN_fit, color = I(line_color), group = Matrix),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 1.4, alpha = 1
  ) +
  # Dark halo behind the piecewise lines.
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = pred_piecewise_ms,
    ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), y = logN_fit, group = interaction(Matrix, segment)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey15", alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 2.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = pred_piecewise_ms,
    ggplot2::aes(x = log10(L_low), y = logN_fit, color = I(line_color), group = interaction(Matrix, segment)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 1.4, alpha = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Model, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = matrix_pal_cpsd, name = "Matrix") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = matrix_pal_cpsd, guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 0.5, `FALSE` = 0.10), guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "Single-slope (headline MLE) vs. two-segment (piecewise) fits by matrix (particle length)",
    subtitle = "Dotted = fitted LOD window boundaries. Faded points = outside LOD window. In the two-segment panel, the break is where each matrix's line visibly bends.",
    x        = expression(log[10] * "(Length, " * mu * "m)"),
    y        = expression(log[10] * (N("">=L)))
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text      = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    panel.border    = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4)
  )

ggsave(cpsd_single_vs_piecewise_plot, filename = "figures/cpsd_single_vs_piecewise_plot.png", width = 13, height = 7, dpi = 300)
cpsd_single_vs_piecewise_plot
```

## 13.3 Piecewise (dual-slope) PSD as a bounding exposure case

The production `correction_factor()` extrapolates a single fitted power-law slope from the measured LOD window down to the 1 um target floor. The two-segment diagnostic above (§13.2) shows the data themselves often prefer a shallower fine-size slope below a break point and a steeper coarse-size slope above it (river ΔAIC in the diagnostic table strongly favors the two-segment model; sediment likewise). Because the sub-floor extrapolation zone (1 um to the fitted LOD) can straddle or sit near that break — and because the fitted critical size `d_c` for river (~36 um) falls inside that 1-50 um extrapolation zone rather than inside the fit window itself — a single coarse slope may not be the right model to extrapolate through that zone. Independent evidence that single power laws mis-extrapolate to small, unmeasured sizes: in the St Louis Estuary, a single power law extrapolated to 1.3-12 particles/L for 5-5000 um while flow cytometry directly measured 600-1,600 particles/L in the same system ([Thomas et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.3c10776)), and [Segur et al. (2026)](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-8524083/v1) find size-aligned 1-5000 um concentrations average ~600x higher than reported values based on single-slope extrapolation. Both are cited as **evidence that single-power-law extrapolation to small sizes is unreliable in general**, not as a validated correction for this dataset.

`correction_factor_piecewise()` (`R/mp_risk_utils.R`, SPEC 2b) implements the two-segment alternative: it integrates dN/dL = k*L^a using the fine-segment differential slope over [1, break_um] and the coarse-segment differential slope over [break_um, 5000], with the coarse segment's density scaled so the two segments meet exactly (are continuous) at `break_um`. The piecewise cumulative slopes from the §13.2 diagnostic are converted to the differential convention (a_psd = a_cpsd - 1) internally via `slope_convention = "cumulative"`, consistent with the SPEC 1c guard. **This is a labeled bounding sensitivity, not a replacement for the single-slope production CF** — the production exposure pipeline (Sections 5-6, 9-10, 12) is unchanged. The 1 um-LOD_low sub-window is unconstrained by data in *both* the single-slope and piecewise case; the piecewise result quantifies structural (model-form) uncertainty in how that unconstrained sub-window is extrapolated, which is not captured by the Gaussian `slope_structural_sd` already added to the fit-uncertainty propagation.

```{r spec2b-piecewise-cf}
piecewise_cf_row <- function(matrix_label, piecewise_row, L_meas_min, L_meas_max) {
  brk <- piecewise_row$piecewise_break_um
  s_lo <- piecewise_row$piecewise_low_a_cpsd
  s_hi <- piecewise_row$piecewise_high_a_cpsd
  if (!is.finite(brk) || !is.finite(s_lo) || !is.finite(s_hi)) {
    return(tibble::tibble(Matrix = matrix_label, break_um = NA_real_, cf_piecewise = NA_real_))
  }
  cf_pw <- correction_factor_piecewise(
    a_low = s_lo, a_high = s_hi, break_um = brk,
    L_meas_min = L_meas_min, L_meas_max = L_meas_max,
    L_tar_min = 1, L_tar_max = 5000,
    slope_convention = "cumulative"
  )
  tibble::tibble(Matrix = matrix_label, break_um = brk, cf_piecewise = cf_pw)
}

pw_river <- piecewise_cf_row("River water", dplyr::filter(critical_piecewise_tbl, Matrix == "River water"), L_meas_min_use, L_meas_max_use)
pw_sed   <- piecewise_cf_row("Sediment",    dplyr::filter(critical_piecewise_tbl, Matrix == "Sediment"),    L_meas_min_use_sed, L_meas_max_use_sed)
pw_ocean <- piecewise_cf_row("Ocean water", dplyr::filter(critical_piecewise_tbl, Matrix == "Ocean water"), L_meas_min_ocean, L_meas_max_ocean)

# Piecewise sensitivity is an exposure-only (CF/EED) effect: apply the single
# piecewise CF point estimate to the raw per-sample measured concentrations,
# then bootstrap the EED exactly as for the single-slope case. Hazard (haz*)
# is unchanged, so any RQ shift below is attributable to the piecewise CF alone.
set.seed(9401)
eed_boot_piecewise_river <- if (is.finite(pw_river$cf_piecewise)) {
  bootstrap_eed(monitoring_pooled_scope$C_measured_pL * pw_river$cf_piecewise, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
} else NULL
set.seed(9402)
eed_boot_piecewise_sed <- if (is.finite(pw_sed$cf_piecewise)) {
  bootstrap_eed(monitoring_sed$C_measured_pkg * pw_sed$cf_piecewise, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
} else NULL
set.seed(9403)
eed_boot_piecewise_ocean <- if (is.finite(pw_ocean$cf_piecewise)) {
  bootstrap_eed(monitoring_ocean$C_measured_pL * pw_ocean$cf_piecewise, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
} else NULL

set.seed(9411)
risk_draws_piecewise_river <- if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_river)) {
  # Two-segment exposure vs the pooled single-slope hazard: the one documented
  # ALIGNMENT RULE exception (PSSDplusplus cannot take a two-segment PSD).
  draw_rq_mc1d(haz_pooled, eed_boot_piecewise_river$q50, n_risk = n_risk)
} else NULL
risk_summary_piecewise_river <- if (!is.null(risk_draws_piecewise_river)) summarize_rq(risk_draws_piecewise_river) else NULL

set.seed(9412)
risk_summary_piecewise_sed <- if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_sed)) {
  summarize_rq(draw_rq_mc1d(haz_sed, eed_boot_piecewise_sed$q50, n_risk = n_risk_sed))
} else NULL

set.seed(9413)
risk_draws_piecewise_ocean <- if (!is.null(eed_boot_piecewise_ocean)) {
  draw_rq_mc1d(haz_ocean, eed_boot_piecewise_ocean$q50, n_risk = n_risk_ocean)
} else NULL
risk_summary_piecewise_ocean <- if (!is.null(risk_draws_piecewise_ocean)) summarize_rq(risk_draws_piecewise_ocean) else NULL
```

```{r spec2b-rq-bounding-table}
rq_bounding_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary,                                     Matrix = "River water", Case = "Single-slope (production)"),
  if (!is.null(risk_summary_piecewise_river)) dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_piecewise_river, Matrix = "River water", Case = "Piecewise (bounding)"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_sed,                                 Matrix = "Sediment",    Case = "Single-slope (production)"),
  if (!is.null(risk_summary_piecewise_sed)) dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_piecewise_sed, Matrix = "Sediment",    Case = "Piecewise (bounding)"),
  dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_ocean,                               Matrix = "Ocean water", Case = "Single-slope (production)"),
  if (!is.null(risk_summary_piecewise_ocean)) dplyr::mutate(risk_summary_piecewise_ocean, Matrix = "Ocean water", Case = "Piecewise (bounding)")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(ERM %in% c("Food Dilution", "Tissue Translocation"), HCx == 5) |>
  dplyr::select(Matrix, Case, ERM, RQ_p50, RQ_p95, P_exceed) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Matrix, ERM, Case)

# 95% CI (2.5th-97.5th percentile of the underlying 1D risk draws) for the
# plot's error bars -- summarize_rq() itself only returns p50/p95/p99, so the
# lower bound is computed here directly from each case's already-existing raw
# draws object (river/ocean single-slope: risk_draws/risk_draws_ocean, already
# built in Sections 8/12.4; piecewise: risk_draws_piecewise_river/_ocean,
# saved alongside their summaries above) rather than retrofitting summarize_rq().
rq_ci_from_draws <- function(draws, matrix_label, case_label) {
  if (is.null(draws)) return(NULL)
  draws |>
    dplyr::filter(ERM %in% c("Food Dilution", "Tissue Translocation"), HCx == 5) |>
    dplyr::group_by(ERM) |>
    dplyr::summarise(RQ_p025 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                      RQ_p975 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(Matrix = matrix_label, Case = case_label)
}

rq_bounding_ci <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rq_ci_from_draws(risk_draws,                 "River water", "Single-slope (production)"),
  rq_ci_from_draws(risk_draws_piecewise_river,  "River water", "Piecewise (bounding)"),
  rq_ci_from_draws(risk_draws_ocean,            "Ocean water", "Single-slope (production)"),
  rq_ci_from_draws(risk_draws_piecewise_ocean,  "Ocean water", "Piecewise (bounding)")
)

rq_bounding_tbl <- rq_bounding_tbl |> dplyr::left_join(rq_bounding_ci, by = c("Matrix", "Case", "ERM"))

knitr::kable(
  rq_bounding_tbl, digits = 3,
  caption = paste0(
    "SPEC 2b: Food Dilution / Tissue Translocation HC5 RQ bounding range, single-slope (production) vs. piecewise ",
    "(bounding sensitivity). RQ_p025/RQ_p975 = 95% CI (2.5th-97.5th percentile of the 1D risk draws); not available ",
    "for Sediment (illustrative only, no comparable raw-draws object retained)."
  )
)
```

```{r spec2b-rq-bounding-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
# Sediment excluded entirely (not just labeled illustrative) -- its exposure
# concentration is not a genuine particles/kg-dry-weight value (SPEC 1d), so
# it is not comparable to the River/Ocean RQs even on a log scale.
rq_bounding_dodge <- ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.5)

rq_bounding_plot <- rq_bounding_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(Matrix != "Sediment") |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = Matrix, y = RQ_p50, color = ERM, shape = Case)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(ymin = RQ_p025, ymax = RQ_p975), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.6,
                         position = rq_bounding_dodge, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3.5, position = rq_bounding_dodge) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = ERM_PALETTE, name = "ERM") +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = c("Single-slope (production)" = 16, "Piecewise (bounding)" = 17), name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = "HC5 median RQ [log10 scale]",
    title = "Food Dilution / Tissue Translocation HC5 RQ: single-slope vs. piecewise bounding sensitivity",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = RQ = 1. Bars = 95% CI (2.5th-97.5th percentile of the 1D risk draws). Sediment excluded (illustrative only, SPEC 1d; see Section 13.3 table for its non-comparable value)."
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4))

ggsave(rq_bounding_plot, filename = "figures/rq_bounding_plot.png", width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300)
rq_bounding_plot
```

**Bounding range interpretation.** The table above states, per matrix, the single-slope production RQ alongside the piecewise-sensitivity RQ; whichever is larger sets the upper bound of the sensitivity range and whichever is smaller sets the lower bound. Because the fine-size (sub-break) slope from the §13.2 diagnostic is shallower than the coarse-size slope for the matrices where the two-segment model is favored, the piecewise CF is expected to sit *below* the single-slope CF (less extrapolated mass assigned to the unconstrained 1 um-LOD_low zone) — i.e., the piecewise bound is expected to **narrow** the exposure (and therefore RQ) estimate relative to the single-slope production value, not widen it, for this dataset. This is stated as an expectation to be read against the rendered numbers above, not assumed; if a matrix's piecewise CF instead exceeds the single-slope CF, that reversal is itself informative about how sensitive the conclusion is to the extrapolation model and should be flagged rather than averaged away. Regardless of direction, the single-slope CF remains the production default per the guardrails in the corrective-revision spec; the piecewise result is reported here strictly as a labeled sensitivity bound. **Sediment caveat (SPEC 1d):** the Sediment column/row above is illustrative only, for the same reason noted in Section 13.1/11.3.0 — its exposure concentration is not a genuine particles/kg-dry-weight value.

# 12.5 Methods-robustness and source-attribution analyses (surface water only)

Three additive analyses testing whether the risk conclusion is robust to specific methodological choices (the sub-floor extrapolation, the extrapolation model itself), and whether the river-vs-ocean slope difference has independent support from polymer composition. River and ocean only — sediment is not touched. None of these change the production headline (single-slope C-PSD, `L_tar_min = 1` µm); each is a clearly-labeled sensitivity/robustness addition that reuses the already-computed production hazard/exposure objects wherever possible rather than recomputing them.

## 12.5.1 RQ sensitivity to the extrapolation floor L_tar_min (food dilution)

The production correction factor extrapolates the measured particle count down to `L_tar_min = 1` µm. Food Dilution is volume-weighted, so a power-law explosion of sub-floor particle *number* adds little particle *volume* — the RQ may be far less sensitive to `L_tar_min` than the raw number-based CF implies. This test is only valid if exposure and hazard are evaluated on the same lower size bound, so for each floor the toxicity dataset is filtered to match: a ToMEx record is excluded from a given floor if its own characteristic tested size (`size.length.um.used.for.conversions` for monodisperse records, or the tested range via `size.length.max.um.used.for.conversions` for polydisperse records — the same field `PSSDplusplus::align_data()` itself uses to size-align doses) falls entirely below that floor. Records with a missing characteristic size are excluded rather than imputed. `filter_tox_by_size_floor()` (`R/mp_risk_utils.R`) implements this rule.

At each floor, three things move together: (1) the exposure-side correction factor and EED are recomputed over `[L_tar_min, 5000]` µm; (2) the pSSD++ integration floor (`x1M_set` in `matrix_function()`, `x1D_set` in `run_pssd_pipeline()`) is set to the same `L_tar_min`; and (3) the Food Dilution toxicity records are filtered as above before the hazard alignment is re-derived. The `L_tar_min = 1` µm row reuses the already-computed production CF/EED/hazard objects rather than recomputing an identical result under a new seed (relocate-don't-recompute).

```{r m12-floor-sensitivity, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE, cache.extra=list(n_boot, raw_data_cache_key, as.character(packageVersion("PSSDplusplus")))}
m12_floors <- c(1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 20)

m12_run_one_floor <- function(L_tar_min, matrix_label, monitoring_df, cpsd_fit, alpha_draws,
                               tox_data_base, param_values_base, environments,
                               matrix_extra_args, rave_override_fn, seed_base,
                               prod_cf = NULL, prod_eed = NULL, prod_haz = NULL) {

  tox_data_i  <- filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_base, L_tar_min)
  n_tox_i     <- nrow(tox_data_i)
  n_species_i <- dplyr::n_distinct(tox_data_i$Species)

  na_row <- function(note) {
    tibble::tibble(
      Matrix = matrix_label, L_tar_min = L_tar_min,
      CF_p50 = NA_real_, EED_q50 = NA_real_,
      n_tox_records = n_tox_i, n_species = n_species_i, HC5_median = NA_real_,
      RQ_p50_1D = NA_real_, RQ_p025_1D = NA_real_, RQ_p975_1D = NA_real_, P_exceed_1D = NA_real_,
      RQ_p50_MC2D = NA_real_, P_exceed_MC2D = NA_real_,
      CF_RSD_pct = NA_real_, RQ_p50_RSD_pct = NA_real_, note = note
    )
  }

  if (isTRUE(L_tar_min == 1) && !is.null(prod_cf)) {
    combined_cf_i <- prod_cf
    eed_boot_i    <- prod_eed
    haz_i         <- prod_haz
  } else {
    set.seed(seed_base)
    corr_i <- correct_and_bootstrap_eed(
      monitoring = monitoring_df, conc_col = "C_measured_pL", cpsd_fit = cpsd_fit,
      alpha_draws = alpha_draws, L_tar_min = L_tar_min, L_tar_max = 5000,
      n_draws = 3000, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95), slope_convention = "differential"
    )
    combined_cf_i <- corr_i$combined_cf
    eed_boot_i    <- corr_i$eed_boot

    set.seed(seed_base + 1)
    # matrix_function_safe() (R/mp_risk_utils.R): a local patched copy of
    # PSSDplusplus::matrix_function() -- the installed package's oversample-
    # then-slice logic for upper.tissue.trans.size.um silently under-fills
    # when x1M_set narrows the acceptance window (confirmed failing at
    # x1M_set >= 20 with this analysis's real river parameters); the patch
    # replaces only that block with a draw-until-quota-met loop using the
    # identical rnorm() parameters and filter conditions. See the function's
    # own roxygen comment for the full diagnosis. Installed PSSDplusplus is
    # never modified.
    param_matrix_i <- do.call(
      matrix_function_safe,
      c(list(n_sobol = n_boot, params = param_values_base, upper.tissue.truncation.limit = 500,
             x1M_set = L_tar_min, x2D_set = 5000), matrix_extra_args)
    ) |> rave_override_fn()

    # A high L_tar_min can leave too few (or zero) Food-Dilution-alignable
    # records after PSSDplusplus's own ingestible/size-gating logic runs
    # inside MC_sim_align_parallel(), even when the raw filtered tox_data_i
    # row count looks adequate -- build_haz_df() then has nothing to
    # summarise for that ERM. Caught here rather than crashing the render,
    # per the spec's own guardrail: flag as indicative-only (NA row with a
    # note) rather than treat as a production result.
    pssd_haz <- tryCatch({
      pssd_i <- run_pssd_pipeline(
        tox_data = tox_data_i, param_matrix = param_matrix_i, environments = environments,
        cache_suffix = paste0("m12_", matrix_label, "_", L_tar_min),
        dose_unit = "L", n_sim = n_boot, num_cores = parallel::detectCores() - 2,
        sim = 30, cv_uf = 0.5, rmore_method = "lognormal",
        seed = seed_base + 2, x1D_set = L_tar_min
      )
      haz_try <- build_haz_df(pssd_i$pSSDs, environments[1])
      if (is.null(haz_try) || nrow(haz_try) == 0 ||
          !any(haz_try$ERM == "Food Dilution" & haz_try$HCx == 5)) {
        list(ok = FALSE, note = "pSSD fit returned no Food Dilution HC5 at this floor")
      } else {
        list(ok = TRUE, haz = haz_try)
      }
    }, error = function(e) {
      list(ok = FALSE, note = paste0("pSSD/hazard fit failed: ", conditionMessage(e)))
    })

    if (!pssd_haz$ok) {
      return(na_row(pssd_haz$note))
    }
    haz_i <- pssd_haz$haz
  }

  set.seed(seed_base + 3)
  risk_draws_1d <- draw_rq_mc1d(haz_i, eed_boot_i$q50, n_risk = 1000)
  rs_1d <- summarize_rq(risk_draws_1d) |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5)
  rs_1d_ci <- risk_draws_1d |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5) |>
    dplyr::summarise(RQ_p025 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                      RQ_p975 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))

  mc2d_i <- mc2d_risk(monitoring_df = monitoring_df, combined_cf = combined_cf_i, haz_df = haz_i,
                       n_uncertainty = 100, n_variability = 500, seed = seed_base + 4)
  mc2d_food_hc5_i <- mc2d_i |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5)
  rs_mc2d <- mc2d_food_hc5_i |>
    dplyr::summarise(P_exceed_med = median(P_exceed), RQ_p50_med = median(RQ_p50))

  hc5_i <- haz_i |> dplyr::filter(ERM == "Food Dilution", HCx == 5) |> dplyr::pull(PNEC) |> stats::median()

  # Uncertainty (not variability) at this floor: %RSD of the exposure-side CF
  # draws (correction_factor() output, one value per alpha_draws realization)
  # and %RSD of the outer-loop (uncertainty) RQ_p50 across mc2d_risk()'s
  # n_uncertainty = 100 CF+PNEC draws. Both are dispersion-of-the-estimate
  # measures, not the exposure variability captured by the inner loop --
  # answers "how much does our estimate of the risk move if we re-ran the
  # uncertain inputs," at each L_tar_min.
  cf_rsd_pct     <- 100 * stats::sd(combined_cf_i) / mean(combined_cf_i)
  rq_p50_rsd_pct <- 100 * stats::sd(mc2d_food_hc5_i$RQ_p50) / mean(mc2d_food_hc5_i$RQ_p50)

  tibble::tibble(
    Matrix = matrix_label, L_tar_min = L_tar_min,
    CF_p50 = stats::median(combined_cf_i), EED_q50 = stats::median(eed_boot_i$q50),
    n_tox_records = n_tox_i, n_species = n_species_i, HC5_median = hc5_i,
    RQ_p50_1D = rs_1d$RQ_p50, RQ_p025_1D = rs_1d_ci$RQ_p025, RQ_p975_1D = rs_1d_ci$RQ_p975, P_exceed_1D = rs_1d$P_exceed,
    RQ_p50_MC2D = rs_mc2d$RQ_p50_med, P_exceed_MC2D = rs_mc2d$P_exceed_med,
    CF_RSD_pct = cf_rsd_pct, RQ_p50_RSD_pct = rq_p50_rsd_pct, note = NA_character_
  )
}

rave_override_river <- function(pm) {
  pm |> dplyr::mutate(
    R.ave.water.freshwater = sample(R.ave_vals, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE),
    H_W_ratio.freshwater   = sample(R.ave_vals, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE)
  )
}
rave_override_ocean <- function(pm) {
  pm |> dplyr::mutate(
    R.ave.water.marine     = sample(R.ave_ocean_vals, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE),
    H_W_ratio.water.marine = sample(R.ave_ocean_vals, size = dplyr::n(), replace = TRUE)
  )
}

m12_river_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(m12_floors, function(L) {
  m12_run_one_floor(
    L_tar_min = L, matrix_label = "River water", monitoring_df = monitoring_pooled_scope,
    cpsd_fit = cpsd_fit_all, alpha_draws = alpha, tox_data_base = tox_data,
    param_values_base = param_values, environments = c("Freshwater"),
    matrix_extra_args = list(), rave_override_fn = rave_override_river,
    seed_base = 61000 + round(L * 10), prod_cf = combined_cf_pooled, prod_eed = eed_boot_pooled, prod_haz = haz_pooled
  )
}))

m12_ocean_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(m12_floors, function(L) {
  m12_run_one_floor(
    L_tar_min = L, matrix_label = "Ocean water", monitoring_df = monitoring_ocean,
    cpsd_fit = cpsd_fit_ocean_all, alpha_draws = alpha_ocean, tox_data_base = tox_data_ocean,
    param_values_base = param_values_ocean, environments = c("Marine"),
    matrix_extra_args = list(include_marine_surface_water = TRUE, include_freshwater_surface_water = FALSE,
                              include_marine_sediment = FALSE, include_freshwater_sediment = FALSE),
    rave_override_fn = rave_override_ocean,
    seed_base = 62000 + round(L * 10), prod_cf = combined_cf_ocean, prod_eed = eed_boot_ocean, prod_haz = haz_ocean
  )
}))

m12_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(m12_river_results, m12_ocean_results)

knitr::kable(
  m12_results |> dplyr::select(Matrix, L_tar_min, CF_p50, EED_q50, n_tox_records, n_species,
                                HC5_median, RQ_p50_1D, P_exceed_1D, RQ_p50_MC2D, P_exceed_MC2D, note),
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste0(
    "M1.2: Food Dilution RQ sensitivity to the extrapolation floor L_tar_min, river and ocean, ",
    "with exposure/hazard/tox-record size basis matched at every floor. NA rows (see Note) mean ",
    "the floor left too few Food-Dilution-alignable records for a pSSD++ fit -- indicative only, ",
    "not a production result. CF and RQ %RSD by floor are reported separately in Section 12.5.1.1."
  ),
  col.names = c("Matrix", "L_tar_min (µm)", "CF p50", "EED q50", "n tox records", "n species",
                "HC5 median", "RQ p50 (1D)", "P(RQ>1) (1D)", "RQ p50 (MC2D)", "P(RQ>1) (MC2D)", "Note")
)
```

```{r m12-floor-sensitivity-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
m12_dodge <- ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.5)

m12_plot <- m12_results |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = L_tar_min, y = RQ_p50_1D, color = Matrix)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, position = m12_dodge, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(ymin = RQ_p025_1D, ymax = RQ_p975_1D),
                          width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.6, position = m12_dodge, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, position = m12_dodge, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = m12_floors) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("River water" = "#0072B2", "Ocean water" = "#009E73"), name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = expression(L[tar-min]~"(µm)"),
    y = "Food Dilution HC5 median RQ (1D) [log10 scale]",
    title = "Food Dilution RQ sensitivity to the extrapolation floor",
    subtitle = "Points = median RQ (1D); bars = 95% CI (2.5th-97.5th pctile of the 1D risk draws). Dashed line = RQ = 1."
  ) +
```
