```{r m12-floor-sensitivity-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
ggsave(m12_plot, filename = "figures/m12_floor_sensitivity_plot.png", width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300)
m12_plot
```

**Guardrails and interpretation.** The `L_tar_min = 1` µm row is the production headline and is unchanged by this analysis (reused, not recomputed). Any floor where `n_species` falls below the pSSD++ practical minimum is indicative only — read `n_species` in the table above before interpreting that row's RQ. If the Food Dilution median RQ and P(RQ>1) stay well above 1 across all four floors, the sub-floor extrapolation is not driving the exceedance conclusion (expected, since Food Dilution's volume-weighted dose model damps the sub-floor particle-*number* explosion); if the exceedance instead collapses at a higher floor, the conclusion is sensitive to the 1 µm extrapolation and that dependency should be stated plainly rather than averaged away.

### 12.5.1.1 Does restricting the analysis to sizes closer to the measured range reduce uncertainty?

`L_tar_min = 1` µm is the largest extrapolation below the measured detection window (`r round(cpsd_fit_all$lower_lod_used_um)`–`r round(cpsd_fit_all$upper_lod_um)` µm river, `r round(cpsd_fit_ocean_all$lower_lod_used_um)`–`r round(cpsd_fit_ocean_all$upper_lod_um)` µm ocean); raising the floor shortens that extrapolation. Two dispersion metrics separate this from the *magnitude* sensitivity shown above: (1) `CF_RSD_pct`, the relative standard deviation (%RSD = 100 x SD / mean) of the correction-factor draws themselves (`combined_cf_i`, one value per `alpha_draws` realization) -- a pure exposure-side uncertainty measure; and (2) `RQ_p50_RSD_pct`, the %RSD of the median RQ across `mc2d_risk()`'s `n_uncertainty` = 100 outer-loop draws (each redrawing one CF and one PNEC) -- i.e., how much our *estimate* of the median RQ itself moves if the uncertain inputs were redrawn, isolated from the inner-loop exposure *variability* that `RQ_p50_MC2D` above already integrates over.

```{r m12-uncertainty-vs-floor, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
m12_rsd_table <- m12_results |>
  dplyr::select(Matrix, L_tar_min, CF_RSD_pct, RQ_p50_RSD_pct, n_species, note)

knitr::kable(
  m12_rsd_table, digits = 1,
  caption = paste0(
    "Exposure (CF) and risk-estimate (RQ p50, MC2D outer/uncertainty loop) %RSD by extrapolation floor. ",
    "Lower %RSD = less relative dispersion in the estimate. NA rows are the same data-insufficient floors flagged above."
  ),
  col.names = c("Matrix", "L_tar_min (µm)", "CF %RSD", "RQ p50 %RSD", "n species", "Note")
)
```

```{r m12-uncertainty-vs-floor-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# CF %RSD and RQ p50 %RSD live on very different scales, so RQ %RSD is drawn
# against a secondary axis. ggplot2 has no native second y-scale: the
# standard workaround is to rescale the secondary series onto the primary
# series' numeric range by a single ratio, plot it on the primary axis, then
# add a sec_axis() that applies the inverse transform purely for the axis
# labels -- the data themselves are only ever plotted once, in primary units.
m12_rsd_max_cf <- max(m12_results$CF_RSD_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
m12_rsd_max_rq <- max(m12_results$RQ_p50_RSD_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
m12_rsd_ratio  <- m12_rsd_max_cf / m12_rsd_max_rq

m12_rsd_plot_df <- m12_results |>
  dplyr::select(Matrix, L_tar_min, CF_RSD_pct, RQ_p50_RSD_pct) |>
  dplyr::mutate(RQ_p50_RSD_pct_scaled = RQ_p50_RSD_pct * m12_rsd_ratio)

# linetype is mapped to a fixed per-layer string (not a pivoted column) so
# each layer gets its own unambiguous legend key -- a shared/pivoted linetype
# aes previously produced two legend entries that both rendered as solid
# lines because geom_point() (no linetype of its own) was merged into the
# same guide as geom_line().
m12_rsd_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(m12_rsd_plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = L_tar_min, color = Matrix)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = CF_RSD_pct, linetype = "CF (exposure), left axis"),
                      linewidth = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(y = CF_RSD_pct), size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = RQ_p50_RSD_pct_scaled, linetype = "RQ p50 (uncertainty), right axis"),
                      linewidth = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(y = RQ_p50_RSD_pct_scaled), size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("River water" = "#0072B2", "Ocean water" = "#009E73"), name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("CF (exposure), left axis" = "solid", "RQ p50 (uncertainty), right axis" = "dashed"),
    name = NULL,
    guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.1))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    name = "CF %RSD (left axis)",
    sec.axis = ggplot2::sec_axis(~ . / m12_rsd_ratio, name = "RQ p50 %RSD (right axis)")
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = expression(L[tar-min]~"(µm)"),
    title = "Does a higher extrapolation floor reduce estimate uncertainty?",
    subtitle = "Solid = exposure-side CF %RSD (left axis); dashed = Food Dilution HC5 median-RQ %RSD, MC2D uncertainty (outer) loop (right axis)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.8, "cm"),
    panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4)
  )

ggsave(m12_rsd_plot, filename = "figures/m12_uncertainty_vs_floor_plot.png", width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300)
m12_rsd_plot

m12_rsd_river <- m12_results |> dplyr::filter(Matrix == "River water") |> dplyr::arrange(L_tar_min)
m12_rsd_ocean <- m12_results |> dplyr::filter(Matrix == "Ocean water", !is.na(CF_RSD_pct)) |> dplyr::arrange(L_tar_min)
```

**Interpretation.** For river water, CF %RSD moves from `r round(m12_rsd_river$CF_RSD_pct[1], 1)`% at `L_tar_min` = `r m12_rsd_river$L_tar_min[1]` µm to `r round(m12_rsd_river$CF_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_river)], 1)`% at `r m12_rsd_river$L_tar_min[nrow(m12_rsd_river)]` µm, and RQ p50 %RSD moves from `r round(m12_rsd_river$RQ_p50_RSD_pct[1], 1)`% to `r round(m12_rsd_river$RQ_p50_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_river)], 1)`% over the same range. For ocean water (valid floors only, `r paste(m12_rsd_ocean$L_tar_min, collapse=", ")` µm), CF %RSD moves from `r round(m12_rsd_ocean$CF_RSD_pct[1], 1)`% to `r round(m12_rsd_ocean$CF_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_ocean)], 1)`%, and RQ p50 %RSD from `r round(m12_rsd_ocean$RQ_p50_RSD_pct[1], 1)`% to `r round(m12_rsd_ocean$RQ_p50_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_ocean)], 1)`%. `r if (m12_rsd_river$CF_RSD_pct[nrow(m12_rsd_river)] < m12_rsd_river$CF_RSD_pct[1]) "Restricting the correction factor to sizes closer to the measured window does reduce exposure-side dispersion for river water, consistent with a shorter power-law extrapolation carrying less compounded uncertainty." else "Exposure-side dispersion does not monotonically shrink for river water as the floor is raised, so a shorter extrapolation window is not, by itself, guaranteed to reduce CF uncertainty here -- the alpha draw distribution and its interaction with the floor matter more than extrapolation length alone."` This is a **CF/RQ-estimate dispersion** result, not a data-availability result: it does not by itself justify raising the production floor above `L_tar_min` = 1 µm, because (a) the RQ *magnitude* sensitivity above already shows Food Dilution risk is not being driven by the sub-floor extrapolation, and (b) a higher floor discards real tox and monitoring size range along with the extrapolation, at the species-count cost quantified in Section 12.5.1.2 below and in the `n_species` column here.

### 12.5.1.2 Why does the ocean Food Dilution fit fail above L_tar_min = 10 µm?

```{r m12-ocean-floor-diagnostic, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Why ocean, not river, loses its Food Dilution fit above L_tar_min = 1 um --
# diagnostic only (not part of the m12_results pipeline above). Answers: is
# this a code bug, or a real property of the marine ToMEx subset? Computed
# from the same tox_data / tox_data_ocean / filter_tox_by_size_floor() the
# m12 pipeline itself uses, so the numbers below stay live.
m12_char_size <- function(d) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    d$polydispersity == "polydisperse" & !is.na(d$size.length.max.um.used.for.conversions) ~
      d$size.length.max.um.used.for.conversions,
    d$polydispersity == "monodisperse" & !is.na(d$size.length.um.used.for.conversions) ~
      d$size.length.um.used.for.conversions,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )
}

m12_diag <- list(
  river_sp1   = dplyr::n_distinct(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data, 1)$Species),
  river_sp20  = dplyr::n_distinct(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data, 20)$Species),
  ocean_sp1   = dplyr::n_distinct(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, 1)$Species),
  ocean_sp20  = dplyr::n_distinct(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, 20)$Species),
  ocean_fish1  = sum(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, 1)$Group  == "Fish"),
  ocean_fish20 = sum(filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, 20)$Group == "Fish"),
  river_med_size = stats::median(m12_char_size(tox_data), na.rm = TRUE),
  ocean_med_size = stats::median(m12_char_size(tox_data_ocean), na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

Ocean's larger raw species pool is real (`r dplyr::n_distinct(tox_data_ocean$Species)` marine vs `r dplyr::n_distinct(tox_data$Species)` freshwater species pass the same QC filters before any size floor is applied) but it is concentrated at much smaller tested particle sizes: the marine subset's median characteristic tested size is `r round(m12_diag$ocean_med_size, 1)` µm against `r round(m12_diag$river_med_size, 1)` µm for freshwater, and `r round(100 * mean(tox_data_ocean$polydispersity == "monodisperse"), 0)`% of marine records are monodisperse (small, uniform test beads) versus `r round(100 * mean(tox_data$polydispersity == "monodisperse"), 0)`% for freshwater. Raising the floor to 20 µm therefore removes marine records disproportionately: usable species fall from `r m12_diag$ocean_sp1` to `r m12_diag$ocean_sp20` for ocean (a `r scales::percent(1 - m12_diag$ocean_sp20/m12_diag$ocean_sp1, accuracy = 1)` drop) versus `r m12_diag$river_sp1` to `r m12_diag$river_sp20` for river (`r scales::percent(1 - m12_diag$river_sp20/m12_diag$river_sp1, accuracy = 1)`). Fish records, the single largest marine Food-Dilution-relevant group at 1 µm, collapse from `r m12_diag$ocean_fish1` to `r m12_diag$ocean_fish20` -- almost all marine fish-feeding studies in this ToMEx subset used particles smaller than 20 µm. Once `run_pssd_pipeline()`'s own ingestibility/dose-positive/non-Algae gating runs on top of that, too few marine species remain for `PSSDplusplus` to construct a Food Dilution SSD at all at `L_tar_min` = 20 µm, so `pSSDs[["Tier3_Marine_Food Dilution"]]` is `NULL` and the row is flagged NA rather than fabricated -- this is a genuine data-sparsity limit of the current marine ToMEx subset at larger size floors, not a pipeline defect. The two finer intermediate floors (5, 10 µm) added below still resolve, confirming the failure is specific to the 20 µm floor rather than a broad breakdown of the marine pipeline.

## 12.5.1.3 M2 -- Decomposition of the M1.2 floor effect

**DECOMPOSITION DIAGNOSTIC -- NOT A RISK ESTIMATE.** Section 12.5.1 varies a single control knob, `L_tar_min`, and moves three things at once: (1) the exposure correction-factor extrapolation, (2) the pSSD++ hazard-integration range, and (3) which tox records survive `filter_tox_by_size_floor()` (composition). Because these move together, M1.2 alone cannot attribute the RQ collapse it shows to a mechanism. This section freezes tox composition at a common `L_tar_min = 10` µm reference set (`tox_fixed`) and re-runs the pipeline in two arms that isolate the other two components, then decomposes M1.2's own total collapse into exposure-CF, hazard-integration, and composition contributions in log-RQ space. No production number is touched; every output here is a labeled diagnostic. Per `spec/m2_spec.md`'s own caveat: freezing tox at >= 10 µm is mechanistically conservative for Tissue Translocation specifically, since it removes exactly the small (< 83 µm, and especially < 10 µm) particles most translocation-relevant -- the TT arm below is a lower bound on TT hazard and a diagnostic contrast, not a TT risk estimate.

```{r m2-harness, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
TOX_FIXED_FLOOR <- 10 # µm; the highest M1.2 floor at which both river and ocean Food Dilution SSDs still converge (ocean fails at 20 µm) -- a composition-stable set common to every arm.
tox_fixed_river <- filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data,       TOX_FIXED_FLOOR)
tox_fixed_ocean <- filter_tox_by_size_floor(tox_data_ocean, TOX_FIXED_FLOOR)
m2_floors <- c(1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10) # adds 7.5 µm vs the spec's motivating {1,2.5,5,10} to resolve the 5->10 shoulder; matches m12_floors exactly so M1.2 values need no interpolation.

m2_get_cfg <- function(compartment) {
  if (compartment == "river") {
    list(monitoring_df = monitoring_pooled_scope, cpsd_fit = cpsd_fit_all, alpha_draws = alpha,
         tox_data_base = tox_data, tox_fixed = tox_fixed_river,
         param_values_base = param_values, environments = c("Freshwater"),
         matrix_extra_args = list(), rave_override_fn = rave_override_river, env_key = "Freshwater",
         prod_cf = combined_cf_pooled, prod_eed = eed_boot_pooled, prod_haz = haz_pooled)
  } else {
    list(monitoring_df = monitoring_ocean, cpsd_fit = cpsd_fit_ocean_all, alpha_draws = alpha_ocean,
         tox_data_base = tox_data_ocean, tox_fixed = tox_fixed_ocean,
         param_values_base = param_values_ocean, environments = c("Marine"),
         matrix_extra_args = list(include_marine_surface_water = TRUE, include_freshwater_surface_water = FALSE,
                                   include_marine_sediment = FALSE, include_freshwater_sediment = FALSE),
         rave_override_fn = rave_override_ocean, env_key = "Marine",
         prod_cf = combined_cf_ocean, prod_eed = eed_boot_ocean, prod_haz = haz_ocean)
  }
}

# One pSSD/hazard fit (matrix_function_safe() -> run_pssd_pipeline() -> build_haz_df()),
# tryCatch-wrapped per the M1.2 precedent so a data-insufficient cell reports a
# note instead of crashing the render (spec guardrail: "report the failure
# rather than silently dropping the cell").
m2_compute_hazard <- function(cfg, tox_i, x_haz, cache_tag, seed_hazard) {
  set.seed(seed_hazard)
  param_matrix_i <- do.call(
    matrix_function_safe,
    c(list(n_sobol = n_boot, params = cfg$param_values_base, upper.tissue.truncation.limit = 500,
           x1M_set = x_haz, x2D_set = 5000), cfg$matrix_extra_args)
  ) |> cfg$rave_override_fn()

  tryCatch({
    pssd_i <- run_pssd_pipeline(
      tox_data = tox_i, param_matrix = param_matrix_i, environments = cfg$environments,
      cache_suffix = cache_tag, dose_unit = "L", n_sim = n_boot,
      num_cores = parallel::detectCores() - 2, sim = 30, cv_uf = 0.5, rmore_method = "lognormal",
      seed = seed_hazard, x1D_set = x_haz
    )
    haz_try <- build_haz_df(pssd_i$pSSDs, cfg$env_key)
    if (is.null(haz_try) || nrow(haz_try) == 0) {
      list(ok = FALSE, haz = NULL, note = "pSSD fit returned no hazard rows at this arm/floor")
    } else {
      list(ok = TRUE, haz = haz_try, note = NA_character_)
    }
  }, error = function(e) list(ok = FALSE, haz = NULL, note = paste0("pSSD/hazard fit failed: ", conditionMessage(e))))
}

#' One (compartment, arm, floor) cell of the M2 grid
#'
#' arm "A"        -- composition AND hazard-integration bound frozen at
#'                   TOX_FIXED_FLOOR (tox_fixed, x1M/x1D = 10); only the
#'                   exposure CF floor tracks L_tar_min. Isolates component
#'                   (1), pure exposure-CF/de-extrapolation.
#' arm "B"        -- composition frozen (tox_fixed) but the hazard-integration
#'                   bound now tracks L_tar_min too. Adds component (2),
#'                   hazard-integration-range, on top of Arm A.
#' arm "M12equiv" -- composition ALSO tracks L_tar_min (filter_tox_by_size_floor
#'                   re-applied at every floor), i.e. exactly M1.2's own
#'                   pipeline. Reused directly from the live m12_results object
#'                   for Food Dilution (never recomputed); computed fresh here
#'                   for Tissue Translocation, which M1.2 itself never covered.
m2_run_one <- function(compartment, arm, L_tar_min, seed_exposure, seed_hazard, arm_a_haz_cache) {
  cfg <- m2_get_cfg(compartment)
  tox_i <- if (arm %in% c("A", "B")) cfg$tox_fixed else filter_tox_by_size_floor(cfg$tox_data_base, L_tar_min)
  n_tox_i <- nrow(tox_i)
  n_species_i <- dplyr::n_distinct(tox_i$Species)

  na_row <- function(note) {
    tibble::tibble(
      compartment = compartment, arm = arm, L_tar_min = L_tar_min,
      n_tox_records = n_tox_i, n_species = n_species_i,
      CF_p50 = NA_real_, EED_q50 = NA_real_,
      ERM = NA_character_, HC5_median = NA_real_,
      RQ_p50_1D = NA_real_, RQ_p025_1D = NA_real_, RQ_p975_1D = NA_real_, P_exceed_1D = NA_real_,
      RQ_p50_MC2D = NA_real_, P_exceed_MC2D = NA_real_, note = note,
      risk_draws_1d = list(NULL)
    )
  }

  # Exposure: seed is a function of (compartment, floor) ONLY -- shared across
  # all three arms (m2-grid-run below), never varying by arm, because CF/EED
  # computation is identical logic for every arm (all three track L_tar_min on
  # the exposure side; only the hazard side differs). This is required for
  # M2.1's paired study-inclusion-effect companion panel (Section 12.5.1.3.1):
  # the paired ratio RQ_M12,i/RQ_ArmB,i = HC5_ArmB,i/HC5_M12,i only holds if
  # E_i (exposure draw i) is literally the same value for Arm B and M12equiv
  # at every Monte Carlo index i. No "relocate, don't recompute" shortcut at
  # L_tar_min = 1 here (unlike M1.2's own floor=1 reuse) -- reusing the
  # separately-seeded production EED at that floor would break the pairing
  # exactly where the headline finding lives.
  set.seed(seed_exposure)
  corr_i <- correct_and_bootstrap_eed(
    monitoring = cfg$monitoring_df, conc_col = "C_measured_pL", cpsd_fit = cfg$cpsd_fit,
    alpha_draws = cfg$alpha_draws, L_tar_min = L_tar_min, L_tar_max = 5000,
    n_draws = 3000, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95), slope_convention = "differential"
  )
  combined_cf_i <- corr_i$combined_cf
  eed_boot_i    <- corr_i$eed_boot

  if (arm == "A") {
    # Arm A's hazard is floor-invariant by construction (fixed tox, fixed
    # x1M/x1D = TOX_FIXED_FLOOR regardless of L_tar_min) -- computed once per
    # compartment (below) and reused here, both as a compute-cost saving and
    # as the mechanism that makes Arm A's HC5 bit-identical across floors
    # (acceptance check 2, verified below).
    haz_result <- arm_a_haz_cache[[compartment]]
  } else {
    haz_result <- m2_compute_hazard(
      cfg, tox_i, x_haz = L_tar_min,
      cache_tag = paste0("m2_", compartment, "_", arm, "_", L_tar_min),
      seed_hazard = seed_hazard
    )
  }
  if (!haz_result$ok) return(na_row(haz_result$note))
  haz_i <- haz_result$haz

  # Same shared-seed principle applies to the E-side resampling inside
  # draw_rq_mc1d(): seeding identically (seed_exposure + 1, shared across
  # arms) before each arm's call, given identical eed_boot_i$q50 inputs and
  # identical (ERM, HCx) group iteration order (dplyr::group_by() sorts
  # alphabetically), produces identical E_i draws per ERM group across arms.
  # draw_idx retains draw order so the companion panel can pair rows exactly.
  set.seed(seed_exposure + 1)
  risk_draws_1d <- draw_rq_mc1d(haz_i, eed_boot_i$q50, n_risk = 1000) |>
    dplyr::filter(HCx == 5) |>
    dplyr::group_by(ERM) |>
    dplyr::mutate(draw_idx = dplyr::row_number()) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  rs_1d <- risk_draws_1d |>
    dplyr::group_by(ERM, HCx) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      RQ_p50  = stats::median(RQ), P_exceed = mean(RQ > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      RQ_p025 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), RQ_p975 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # mc2d_risk() resamples the already-computed combined_cf_i/haz_i (no new
  # pSSD fit), so this is cheap relative to the hazard fit above -- included
  # per the spec's Table M2-1 ("Arm A RQ (1D + MC2D med)") and M2.1's caveat 2
  # (metric dependence: the 1D "<1" statement must be checked under MC2D too).
  set.seed(seed_exposure + 2)
  mc2d_i <- mc2d_risk(monitoring_df = cfg$monitoring_df, combined_cf = combined_cf_i, haz_df = haz_i,
                       n_uncertainty = 100, n_variability = 500, seed = seed_exposure + 2)
  rs_mc2d <- mc2d_i |> dplyr::filter(HCx == 5) |> dplyr::group_by(ERM) |>
    dplyr::summarise(RQ_p50_MC2D = stats::median(RQ_p50), P_exceed_MC2D = stats::median(P_exceed), .groups = "drop")

  hc5_by_erm <- haz_i |> dplyr::filter(HCx == 5) |> dplyr::group_by(ERM) |>
    dplyr::summarise(HC5_median = stats::median(PNEC), .groups = "drop")

  # risk_draws_1d nested as a per-ERM list-column so the companion panel
  # (Section 12.5.1.3.1) can unnest and pair Arm B / M12equiv draws by
  # (compartment, ERM, L_tar_min, draw_idx) without any new pSSD computation.
  draws_nested <- risk_draws_1d |> dplyr::group_by(ERM) |> tidyr::nest() |> dplyr::rename(risk_draws_1d = data)

  rs_1d |>
    dplyr::left_join(hc5_by_erm, by = "ERM") |>
    dplyr::left_join(rs_mc2d, by = "ERM") |>
    dplyr::left_join(draws_nested, by = "ERM") |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      compartment = compartment, arm = arm, L_tar_min = L_tar_min,
      n_tox_records = n_tox_i, n_species = n_species_i,
      CF_p50 = stats::median(combined_cf_i), EED_q50 = stats::median(eed_boot_i$q50),
      ERM = ERM, HC5_median = HC5_median,
      RQ_p50_1D = RQ_p50, RQ_p025_1D = RQ_p025, RQ_p975_1D = RQ_p975, P_exceed_1D = P_exceed,
      RQ_p50_MC2D = RQ_p50_MC2D, P_exceed_MC2D = P_exceed_MC2D, note = NA_character_,
      risk_draws_1d = risk_draws_1d
    )
}
```

```{r m2-grid-run, cache=TRUE, cache.extra=list(n_boot, raw_data_cache_key, as.character(packageVersion("PSSDplusplus"))), message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
invisible(gc())   # long production sessions run close to the memory limit
arm_a_haz_cache <- list(
  river = m2_compute_hazard(m2_get_cfg("river"), tox_fixed_river, TOX_FIXED_FLOOR, "m2_armA_haz_river", seed_hazard = 81011),
  ocean = m2_compute_hazard(m2_get_cfg("ocean"), tox_fixed_ocean, TOX_FIXED_FLOOR, "m2_armA_haz_ocean", seed_hazard = 81021)
)

m2_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  compartment = c("river", "ocean"),
  arm         = c("A", "B", "M12equiv"),
  L_tar_min   = m2_floors
)

m2_results <- purrr::pmap_dfr(m2_grid, function(compartment, arm, L_tar_min) {
  comp_idx  <- match(compartment, c("river", "ocean"))
  arm_idx   <- match(arm, c("A", "B", "M12equiv"))
  floor_idx <- match(L_tar_min, m2_floors)
  # seed_exposure deliberately excludes arm_idx (shared across arms -- see the
  # m2-harness chunk's comment on why Arm B / M12equiv need identical E draws).
  seed_exposure <- 81000 + comp_idx * 10000 + floor_idx * 10
  seed_hazard   <- 81000 + comp_idx * 10000 + arm_idx * 1000 + floor_idx * 10 + 1
  m2_run_one(compartment, arm, L_tar_min, seed_exposure, seed_hazard, arm_a_haz_cache)
})
```

```{r m2-ref-tables, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Food Dilution M1.2 reference: read the ALREADY-RENDERED, live M1.2 result
# directly from m12_results (Section 12.5.1) -- never re-derived, per the
# spec's explicit "do not re-run M1.2" instruction and this document's
# no-retyped-literals convention. Tissue Translocation has no M1.2 curve in
# this document (M1.2 was scoped to Food Dilution only, per its own spec), so
# for TT the "M1.2-equivalent" reference is M2's own tox-tracking M12equiv
# arm. Carries the RQ point estimate + 1D 95% CI + MC2D median so the
# scenario figure (Section 12.5.1.3.1) and the decomposition (Section
# 12.5.1.3.5) both draw from one function instead of two separate constructions.
bind_m12_reference <- function() {
  fd <- m12_results |>
    dplyr::filter(L_tar_min %in% m2_floors, is.na(note)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      compartment = ifelse(Matrix == "River water", "river", "ocean"),
      ERM = "Food Dilution", L_tar_min,
      RQ_p50 = RQ_p50_1D, RQ_lo = RQ_p025_1D, RQ_hi = RQ_p975_1D, RQ_mc2d = RQ_p50_MC2D, HC5 = HC5_median
    )
  tt <- m2_results |>
    dplyr::filter(arm == "M12equiv", ERM == "Tissue Translocation", !is.na(RQ_p50_1D)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(compartment, ERM, L_tar_min,
                      RQ_p50 = RQ_p50_1D, RQ_lo = RQ_p025_1D, RQ_hi = RQ_p975_1D, RQ_mc2d = RQ_p50_MC2D, HC5 = HC5_median)
  dplyr::bind_rows(fd, tt)
}

m12_ref_full <- bind_m12_reference()
m12_ref <- m12_ref_full |> dplyr::transmute(compartment, ERM, L_tar_min, RQ_m12 = RQ_p50)

arm_a_ref <- m2_results |> dplyr::filter(arm == "A", !is.na(RQ_p50_1D)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(compartment, ERM, L_tar_min, RQ_A = RQ_p50_1D)
arm_b_ref <- m2_results |> dplyr::filter(arm == "B", !is.na(RQ_p50_1D)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(compartment, ERM, L_tar_min, RQ_B = RQ_p50_1D)

m2_panel_labels <- c(river = "River", ocean = "Ocean")
```

```{r m2-decomposition-data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Three-way decomposition, computed here (data only -- Table M2-2 and the
# fold-contribution table are DISPLAYED later, in the relegated Section
# 12.5.1.3.5, but the underlying numbers are needed by the PROMOTED
# interpretation in 12.5.1.3.1 too, so the arithmetic lives in one place):
#   dlogRQ_total(f)       = logRQ_M1.2(f)  - logRQ_M1.2(10)   [[from the live M1.2/M12equiv reference]]
#   dlogRQ_exposureCF(f)  = logRQ_ArmA(f)  - logRQ_ArmA(10)   [[pure exposure-CF/de-extrapolation]]
#   dlogRQ_hazardInteg(f) = logRQ_ArmB(f)  - logRQ_ArmA(f)    [[hazard-integration-range effect]]
#   dlogRQ_composition(f) = logRQ_M1.2(f)  - logRQ_ArmB(f)    [[study-filtration/composition residual]]
m2_decomp <- m12_ref |>
  dplyr::inner_join(arm_a_ref, by = c("compartment", "ERM", "L_tar_min")) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(arm_b_ref, by = c("compartment", "ERM", "L_tar_min")) |>
  dplyr::filter(RQ_m12 > 0, RQ_A > 0, RQ_B > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(logRQ_m12 = log10(RQ_m12), logRQ_A = log10(RQ_A), logRQ_B = log10(RQ_B)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(compartment, ERM) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    logRQ_m12_ref = logRQ_m12[L_tar_min == TOX_FIXED_FLOOR][1],
    logRQ_A_ref   = logRQ_A[L_tar_min == TOX_FIXED_FLOOR][1]
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dlogRQ_total       = logRQ_m12 - logRQ_m12_ref,
    dlogRQ_exposureCF  = logRQ_A - logRQ_A_ref,
    dlogRQ_hazardInteg = logRQ_B - logRQ_A,
    dlogRQ_composition = logRQ_m12 - logRQ_B,
    residual           = dlogRQ_total - (dlogRQ_exposureCF + dlogRQ_hazardInteg + dlogRQ_composition)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(-logRQ_m12_ref, -logRQ_A_ref)

# fold_* = 10^(dlogRQ) directly (NOT negated): dlogRQ_total(1) = logRQ(1) -
# logRQ(10), and RQ(1) >> RQ(10) (RQ collapses as the floor rises), so
# dlogRQ_total(1) is large and POSITIVE -- 10^(dlogRQ_total) > 1 correctly
# represents "RQ is this many times higher at 1 µm than at 10 µm," i.e. the
# collapse magnitude the spec's motivating "~100-130x" language means.
m2_fold_summary <- m2_decomp |>
  dplyr::filter(L_tar_min == min(m2_floors)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fold_total       = 10^(dlogRQ_total),
    fold_exposureCF  = 10^(dlogRQ_exposureCF),
    fold_hazardInteg = 10^(dlogRQ_hazardInteg),
    fold_composition = 10^(dlogRQ_composition)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(compartment, ERM, fold_total, fold_exposureCF, fold_hazardInteg, fold_composition)
```

### 12.5.1.3.1 Study inclusion, not sub-10 µm extrapolation, drives the exceedance

Two of M2's three arms are size-coherent -- exposure and hazard are rescaled *together* to the identical `[L_tar_min, 5000]` µm range at every floor -- and their difference isolates the study-inclusion (composition) effect cleanly, with no size-basis mismatch: **Arm B** (tox composition frozen at `r TOX_FIXED_FLOOR` µm; only which studies are SSD members is held fixed) versus **M1.2/M12equiv** (tox composition also tracks the floor, i.e. exactly the production/M1.2 pipeline). Arm A does not appear here -- see Section 12.5.1.3.5 for why its absolute values are not physically meaningful on their own.

```{r m2-scenario-data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
scenario_levels <- c("Study set fixed (>=10 µm tox)", "Study set tracks floor (production)")

m2_scenario_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  m2_results |> dplyr::filter(arm == "B", !is.na(RQ_p50_1D)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(compartment, ERM, L_tar_min,
                      RQ_p50 = RQ_p50_1D, RQ_lo = RQ_p025_1D, RQ_hi = RQ_p975_1D,
                      RQ_mc2d = RQ_p50_MC2D, HC5 = HC5_median, scenario = scenario_levels[1]),
  m12_ref_full |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = scenario_levels[2])
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenario_levels))

# Paired study-inclusion effect (companion panel): Arm B and M12equiv share
# IDENTICAL exposure draws at each (compartment, floor) -- the m2-harness
# chunk seeds correct_and_bootstrap_eed() and draw_rq_mc1d()'s E-sampling
# identically across arms for exactly this reason -- so pairing by draw_idx
# cancels the exposure term exactly:
#   RQ_M12,i / RQ_ArmB,i = (E_i / H_M12,i) / (E_i / H_ArmB,i) = H_ArmB,i / H_M12,i
m2_paired_draws <- m2_results |>
  dplyr::filter(arm %in% c("B", "M12equiv"), !is.na(RQ_p50_1D)) |>
  dplyr::select(compartment, arm, L_tar_min, ERM, risk_draws_1d) |>
  tidyr::unnest(risk_draws_1d)

paired_ratio_df <- m2_paired_draws |>
  dplyr::select(compartment, arm, L_tar_min, ERM, draw_idx, H) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = H, names_prefix = "H_") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(H_B), !is.na(H_M12equiv)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = H_B / H_M12equiv) |>
  dplyr::group_by(compartment, ERM, L_tar_min) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    ratio_p50  = stats::median(ratio),
    ratio_p025 = stats::quantile(ratio, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    ratio_p975 = stats::quantile(ratio, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_paired   = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r m2-scenario-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Both ERMs shown (rows) x both compartments (columns), scenario as color.
# Food Dilution is the primary/pre-registered finding; Tissue Translocation
# carries the >= 10 µm composition-freeze caveat (Section 12.5.1.3's intro,
# Section 12.5.1's M12equiv note) in both rows since it's now shown directly
# rather than relegated to a second figure.
m2_scenario_plot <- m2_scenario_df |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = L_tar_min, y = RQ_p50, color = scenario, group = scenario)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.5), na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(ymin = RQ_lo, ymax = RQ_hi), width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.6,
                         position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.5), na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.5), na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = m2_floors) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(ERM ~ compartment, labeller = ggplot2::labeller(compartment = m2_panel_labels), scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("#C87A8A", "#00A396"), name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = expression(L[tar-min]~"(µm)"), y = "HC5 median RQ (1D) [log10]",
    title = "Study inclusion, not sub-10 µm extrapolation, drives the exceedance",
    subtitle = stringr::str_wrap(
      "Both curves rise toward 1 µm (both contain size extrapolation) -- the effect of interest is the GAP between them, not either curve's rise.",
      width = 95
    ),
    caption = stringr::str_wrap(
      "Rows: ERM. Columns: compartment. Tissue Translocation's \"tracks floor\" curve carries the >= 10 µm composition-freeze caveat (Section 12.5.1.3) -- a lower bound on TT hazard, not a TT risk estimate.",
      width = 110
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
                 plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50", hjust = 0))

ggsave(m2_scenario_plot, filename = "figures/m2_scenario_plot.png", width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
m2_scenario_plot
```

```{r m2-interp-text, echo=FALSE}
.m2_river_fd_1 <- function(df) df |> dplyr::filter(compartment == "river", ERM == "Food Dilution", L_tar_min == min(m2_floors))
.m2_river_fd_10 <- function(df) df |> dplyr::filter(compartment == "river", ERM == "Food Dilution", L_tar_min == TOX_FIXED_FLOOR)

m2_armB_river_1  <- m2_results |> dplyr::filter(arm == "B") |> .m2_river_fd_1()
m2_armB_river_10 <- m2_results |> dplyr::filter(arm == "B") |> .m2_river_fd_10()
m2_m12_river_1   <- m12_ref_full |> .m2_river_fd_1()
m2_fold_river    <- m2_fold_summary |> dplyr::filter(compartment == "river", ERM == "Food Dilution")
m2_armB_ocean_1  <- m2_results |> dplyr::filter(arm == "B", compartment == "ocean", ERM == "Food Dilution", L_tar_min == min(m2_floors))
m2_m12_ocean_1   <- m12_ref_full |> dplyr::filter(compartment == "ocean", ERM == "Food Dilution", L_tar_min == min(m2_floors))

m2_have_core <- nrow(m2_armB_river_1) == 1 && nrow(m2_armB_river_10) == 1 && nrow(m2_m12_river_1) == 1 && nrow(m2_fold_river) == 1

m2_interp_main <- if (m2_have_core) {
  armB_below1 <- m2_armB_river_1$RQ_p50_1D < 1
  m12_above1  <- m2_m12_river_1$RQ_p50 > 1
  crossing_phrase <- if (armB_below1 && m12_above1) {
    "The 1 µm-floor exceedance is therefore created by admitting <10 µm-tested studies into the food-dilution SSD (a hazard/HC5 effect), not by coherent sub-10 µm extrapolation."
  } else if (!armB_below1) {
    "Here the size-coherent (Arm B) river Food Dilution RQ is already >= 1 at a 1 µm floor even with the study set fixed, so -- unlike the pre-registered B/E expectation -- coherent extrapolation alone is sufficient for exceedance in this render; study inclusion is an additional, not the sole, driver."
  } else {
    "Here neither scenario's river Food Dilution RQ reaches 1 at a 1 µm floor in this render, so the production exceedance is not reproduced by either size-coherent path alone; see Table M2-1 (Section 12.5.1.3.5) for the full picture."
  }
  paste0(
    "With both exposure and hazard rescaled coherently to a common [L_tar_min, 5000] µm range but the toxicity ",
    "study set held fixed (Arm B), the river Food Dilution RQ at a 1 µm exposure floor is ",
    round(m2_armB_river_1$RQ_p50_1D, 3), " (1D) -- ", if (armB_below1) "below 1" else "at or above 1",
    ". Allowing the study set to open as the floor drops (M12/production) collapses the Food Dilution HC5 from ~",
    round(m2_armB_river_10$HC5_median, 0), " to ~", round(m2_m12_river_1$HC5, 0), " and raises the RQ to ",
    round(m2_m12_river_1$RQ_p50, 3), ". ", crossing_phrase
  )
} else {
  "M2.1's river Food Dilution scenario rows were not fully available at this render budget (see acceptance-check/NA-row notes in Section 12.5.1.3.5)."
}

m2_interp_caveat1 <- if (m2_have_core) {
  exp_larger <- m2_fold_river$fold_exposureCF > m2_fold_river$fold_composition
  paste0(
    "**Magnitude vs threshold-crossing.** Sub-10 µm exposure de-extrapolation is not negligible (river Food Dilution exposure-CF fold ",
    round(m2_fold_river$fold_exposureCF, 2), "x vs composition fold ", round(m2_fold_river$fold_composition, 2), "x; ",
    if (exp_larger) "it is the larger single lever by magnitude). It fails to cross 1 only because it operates on a fixed >=10 µm study set with a very low baseline RQ. "
    else "composition is the larger lever by magnitude as well as the one that decides threshold-crossing). ",
    "Moving the hazard-integration range with the floor contributes a fold of ", round(m2_fold_river$fold_hazardInteg, 2), "x",
    if (m2_fold_river$fold_hazardInteg < 1) " (below 1: aligning the hazard to the lower floor partly offsets the collapse)" else "",
    ". Read this as \"study inclusion is decisive for threshold-crossing,\" never as \"extrapolation is irrelevant.\""
  )
} else ""

m2_interp_caveat2 <- if (m2_have_core && nrow(m2_armB_ocean_1) == 1 && nrow(m2_m12_ocean_1) == 1) {
  ocean_armB_le1 <- m2_armB_ocean_1$RQ_p50_1D <= 1 && m2_armB_ocean_1$RQ_p50_MC2D <= 1
  paste0(
    "**Metric dependence.** ",
    if (m2_armB_river_1$RQ_p50_1D < 1) "The clean \"<1 without study inclusion\" statement is strictly true in 1D for the river; "
    else paste0("In this render the river Arm B Food Dilution RQ is not below 1 in 1D (", round(m2_armB_river_1$RQ_p50_1D, 3), "), so the \"<1 without study inclusion\" statement does not hold; "),
    "under MC2D the river Arm B Food Dilution RQ is ", round(m2_armB_river_1$RQ_p50_MC2D, 3), " versus M12's ",
    round(m2_m12_river_1$RQ_mc2d, 3), ". Ocean Arm B ", if (ocean_armB_le1) "stays <= 1 under both metrics" else "does not stay <= 1 under both metrics in this render (see Table M2-1)",
    " (ocean Arm B 1D = ", round(m2_armB_ocean_1$RQ_p50_1D, 3), ", MC2D = ", round(m2_armB_ocean_1$RQ_p50_MC2D, 3), ")."
  )
} else ""
```

`r m2_interp_main` `r m2_interp_caveat1` `r m2_interp_caveat2` This is a pre-registered hypothesis test (`spec/m2_spec.md` Section 4.1; reframed for presentation by `spec/m21.md`), not a tuned conclusion -- the rendered numbers above are reported regardless of which way they fall. Tissue Translocation's M12equiv reference (computed fresh here, since M1.2 itself never covered TT) carries the >= `r TOX_FIXED_FLOOR` µm composition-freeze caveat throughout: it is a lower bound on TT hazard, not a TT risk estimate. Mechanistically, food dilution is a large-particle (volume/gut-filling) mechanism while small particles preferentially drive translocation (Section 12.5.1's M1.1 framing); admitting small-particle studies into the volume-based food-dilution SSD is the plausible reason the HC5 collapses when the study set is allowed to track the floor, though this analysis tests the *effect*, not that specific *mechanism*, directly.

```{r m2-scenario-caption, echo=FALSE}
m2_cap_river_1 <- list(
  armB = m2_armB_river_1, armB10 = m2_armB_river_10, m12 = m2_m12_river_1,
  gap_fold = if (m2_have_core) round(m2_m12_river_1$RQ_p50 / m2_armB_river_1$RQ_p50_1D, 0) else NA_real_,
  gap_mc2d = if (m2_have_core) round(m2_m12_river_1$RQ_mc2d / m2_armB_river_1$RQ_p50_MC2D, 1) else NA_real_
)
m2_caption_text <- if (m2_have_core) {
  paste0(
    "**Figure.** The Food Dilution risk exceedance is created by toxicity-study inclusion, not by sub-10 µm size ",
    "extrapolation. Median Food Dilution risk quotient (RQ, 1D) versus the lower size floor L_tar_min, faceted by ",
    "compartment; points = median, bars = 95% CI (2.5th-97.5th percentile of the 1D risk draws); dashed line RQ = 1. ",
    "Blue (\"study set fixed >=10 µm\") rescales exposure and hazard coherently to [L_tar_min, 5000] µm but holds ",
    "SSD membership fixed; orange (\"study set tracks floor\") is the production/M1.2 pipeline, which additionally ",
    "admits studies tested below the floor. Both scenarios rise as the floor decreases -- that shared rise is coherent ",
    "size extrapolation, present in both. The effect of interest is the vertical gap between the curves: at a 1 µm ",
    "floor the river RQ is ", round(m2_cap_river_1$armB$RQ_p50_1D, 3), " with the study set fixed but ",
    round(m2_cap_river_1$m12$RQ_p50, 3), " when it tracks the floor (a ", m2_cap_river_1$gap_fold,
    "x study-inclusion effect), because the food-dilution HC5 collapses from ~", round(m2_cap_river_1$armB10$HC5_median, 0),
    " to ~", round(m2_cap_river_1$m12$HC5, 0), " particles/L when <10 µm-tested studies enter the SSD. Coherent ",
    "extrapolation alone leaves the river RQ ", if (m2_cap_river_1$armB$RQ_p50_1D < 1) "below 1 (1D)" else "at or above 1 (1D)",
    "; under MC2D the fixed-set river RQ is ", round(m2_cap_river_1$armB$RQ_p50_MC2D, 3), ", ~",
    m2_cap_river_1$gap_mc2d, "x below the tracking scenario. Diagnostic of model behavior -- the production risk ",
    "characterization is unchanged."
  )
} else {
  "Caption unavailable: core river Food Dilution scenario rows were not available at this render budget."
}
```

`r m2_caption_text`

### 12.5.1.3.2 Why Arm A's absolute values don't matter: the HC5-cancellation identity

Because the exposure-CF term is a difference of two Arm-A quantities that share the identical pinned HC5 (Arm A's hazard is computed once per compartment and reused at every floor -- Section 12.5.1.3.5's acceptance check 2), the HC5 divides out algebraically: ΔlogRQ_exposureCF(f) = log₁₀\[EED(f)/EED(10)\]. Arm A's non-physical absolute RQ (exposure and hazard deliberately aligned to *different* size ranges) never survives this subtraction -- only a pure exposure ratio does.

```{r m2-hc5-cancel-check, echo=FALSE}
eed_armA_river_1  <- m2_results |> dplyr::filter(compartment == "river", arm == "A", ERM == "Food Dilution", L_tar_min == min(m2_floors)) |> dplyr::pull(EED_q50)
eed_armA_river_10 <- m2_results |> dplyr::filter(compartment == "river", arm == "A", ERM == "Food Dilution", L_tar_min == TOX_FIXED_FLOOR) |> dplyr::pull(EED_q50)
m2_eed_ratio_check <- if (length(eed_armA_river_1) == 1 && length(eed_armA_river_10) == 1 && eed_armA_river_10 > 0) {
  eed_armA_river_1 / eed_armA_river_10
} else NA_real_
m2_exposureCF_dlog_check <- m2_decomp |> dplyr::filter(compartment == "river", ERM == "Food Dilution", L_tar_min == min(m2_floors)) |> dplyr::pull(dlogRQ_exposureCF)
```

Verified against the raw exposure: river Food Dilution EED q50 is `r round(eed_armA_river_1, 3)` at 1 µm and `r round(eed_armA_river_10, 3)` at `r TOX_FIXED_FLOOR` µm -- a ratio of `r round(m2_eed_ratio_check, 1)`x, matching the reported exposure-CF fold (`r round(10^m2_exposureCF_dlog_check, 1)`x, Section 12.5.1.3.5) within Monte Carlo noise (ΔlogRQ_exposureCF = `r round(m2_exposureCF_dlog_check, 3)` at the 1 µm river Food Dilution cell).

### 12.5.1.3.5 Sub-decomposition of the coherent trajectory (supplementary)

**Arm A is a diagnostic device only.** Its absolute RQ is non-physical (exposure and hazard are deliberately aligned to different size ranges: exposure over `[L_tar_min, 5000]` but hazard pinned to `[`r TOX_FIXED_FLOOR`, 5000]`). It appears in the decomposition below solely as the difference ΔlogRQ_exposureCF = logRQ_A(f) − logRQ_A(10), in which the pinned HC5 cancels exactly (Section 12.5.1.3.2), leaving a pure exposure ratio. **It is never a risk estimate.** Retained in full here, under this explicit flag, for auditability.

```{r m2-acceptance-check-2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# across every floor for a given compartment x ERM, since Arm A's hazard is
# computed once (arm_a_haz_cache above) and reused, not re-derived per floor.
# Holds unconditionally -- it is a property of the harness wiring, not of MC
# sample size, so it is NOT gated on is_production_budget the way the
# freeze-point/closure checks below are.
m2_armA_hc5_check <- m2_results |>
  dplyr::filter(arm == "A", !is.na(HC5_median)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(compartment, ERM) |>
  dplyr::summarise(hc5_range = max(HC5_median) - min(HC5_median), n_floors = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(m2_armA_hc5_check, digits = 6,
             caption = "M2 acceptance check 2: Arm A HC5 range across floors (must be exactly 0).")

stopifnot(
  "M2 acceptance check 2 FAILED: Arm A HC5 is not flat across floors -- harness mis-wired" =
    all(m2_armA_hc5_check$hc5_range == 0)
)
```

```{r m2-acceptance-checks-1-3, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (is_production_budget) {
  m2_max_resid <- max(abs(m2_decomp$residual), na.rm = TRUE)
  m2_tol <- 0.3 # log10 units (~2x); generous for independently-seeded MC noise, tight enough to catch a genuine multi-order-of-magnitude wiring error
  cat("M2 acceptance checks (production budget, n_boot =", n_boot, "):\n")
  cat("  Check 1 (freeze-point coincidence) & check 3 (decomposition closure) share one quantity here (see note above): max|residual| =",
      signif(m2_max_resid, 3), "log10 units (tolerance", m2_tol, ").\n")
  stopifnot(
    "M2 acceptance checks 1/3 FAILED: freeze-point coincidence / decomposition closure residual exceeds tolerance -- see m2_decomp" =
      m2_max_resid < m2_tol
  )
  cat("M2 acceptance checks 1 and 3 passed.\n")
} else {
  message("M2 acceptance checks 1 and 3 (freeze-point coincidence, decomposition closure) skipped: dev-scale render (n_boot = ",
          n_boot, " < 1000); MC noise is too large relative to the tolerance at this budget. Re-check at the production budget.")
}

# Check 4 (sign sanity, spec Section 2.5): the spec states "exposure-CF
# component should be negative ... RQ falls as floor rises." Under THIS
# section's delta-vs-10-µm-reference parameterization (dlogRQ_exposureCF(f) =
# logRQ_A(f) - logRQ_A(10)), "RQ falls as floor rises" means RQ_A(f) > RQ_A(10)
# for every floor f < 10 µm (more sub-floor extrapolation at a lower floor ->
# higher CF -> higher EED -> higher RQ, holding hazard fixed as Arm A does) --
# i.e. dlogRQ_exposureCF(f) should be POSITIVE for f < 10, not negative; the
# spec's "negative" describes the trend as the floor itself increases, not
# the sign in this fixed-reference-point delta. Reported, not gated (the
# spec constrains this component's sign informationally; only composition's
# sign is explicitly left unconstrained -- but forcing a stopifnot() here
# would just be re-deriving arithmetic already guaranteed by
# correction_factor()'s own monotonicity, not new evidence about the harness).
m2_sign_check <- m2_decomp |>
  dplyr::filter(L_tar_min != TOX_FIXED_FLOOR) |>
  dplyr::summarise(frac_expected_sign = mean(dlogRQ_exposureCF > 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
cat("Sign sanity: exposure-CF component has the expected sign (RQ_A(f) > RQ_A(10) for f <", TOX_FIXED_FLOOR, "µm) for",
    scales::percent(m2_sign_check$frac_expected_sign, accuracy = 1), "of non-reference rows.\n")
```

**Guardrails.** No production headline number is affected by this section (M2 reuses the same underlying `correct_and_bootstrap_eed()` / `matrix_function_safe()` / `run_pssd_pipeline()` / `mc2d_risk()` functions M1.2 already uses, in new diagnostic configurations; it does not modify the production `L_tar_min = 1`, fully-tracking pipeline). Arm A deliberately mismatches the exposure and hazard size bases -- every Arm A number above is a diagnostic, not a valid stand-alone risk quotient; Arm B numbers, by contrast, are legitimate size-coherent risk quotients (just not the production headline, since composition is deliberately held fixed). Sediment is not touched.

## 12.5.2 Model-selection robustness: MLE and a tapered/lognormal small-end model

Distinct from the slope-estimator question (Section 4.1 and 13.7): this section asks how much the *risk result* depends on the sub-floor extrapolation model, given Segur et al.'s caveat that any power-law method extrapolates below the measured range, and marine-surface literature suggesting the true small-end particle-size distribution may roll off (fewer small particles than a single power law implies) rather than continue as one power law to 1 µm.

Three models are fit to each matrix's pooled ("all" shapes) particle-length data: (a) the production headline fit (fixed-window MLE; carried through for comparison, not refit here); (b) an MLE power law (`poweRlaw::conpl`), with `xmin` chosen by minimizing the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic and a goodness-of-fit bootstrap p-value ([Clauset, Shalizi & Newman 2009](https://doi.org/10.1137/070710111); power law rejected if p < 0.1); and (c) a lognormal small-end alternative (`poweRlaw::conlnorm`) fit at the *same* `xmin` as the MLE power law, compared to it via a Vuong likelihood-ratio test (`compare_distributions()`). Ocean fiber (5 populated C-PSD bins; Section 12.1.1) is excluded from MLE fitting as too sparse for a stable tail fit.

```{r m13-model-fits, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
m13_fit_one_matrix <- function(length_vec, matrix_label, seed) {
  length_vec <- length_vec[is.finite(length_vec) & length_vec > 0]

  m_pl <- poweRlaw::conpl$new(length_vec)
  est  <- poweRlaw::estimate_xmin(m_pl)
  m_pl$setXmin(est)

  set.seed(seed)
  bp <- poweRlaw::bootstrap_p(m_pl, no_of_sims = 100, threads = 1, seed = seed)

  m_ln <- poweRlaw::conlnorm$new(length_vec)
  m_ln$setXmin(m_pl$getXmin())
  m_ln$setPars(poweRlaw::estimate_pars(m_ln))

  comp <- poweRlaw::compare_distributions(m_pl, m_ln)

  list(
    matrix_label = matrix_label,
    n_total = length(length_vec),
    xmin = est$xmin, ntail = est$ntail, alpha_mle = m_pl$pars,
    KS_D = est$gof, bootstrap_p = bp$p,
    meanlog = m_ln$pars[1], sdlog = m_ln$pars[2],
    vuong_stat = comp$test_statistic, vuong_p = comp$p_two_sided
  )
}

m13_river_fit <- m13_fit_one_matrix(raw_particles_river$length_um, "River water", seed = 71001)
m13_ocean_fit <- m13_fit_one_matrix(raw_particles_ocean$length_um, "Ocean water", seed = 71002)

m13_fit_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list(m13_river_fit, m13_ocean_fit), function(f) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Matrix = f$matrix_label, n_total = f$n_total, xmin_um = round(f$xmin, 1), n_tail = f$ntail,
    alpha_MLE = round(f$alpha_mle, 3), KS_D = round(f$KS_D, 4), bootstrap_p = round(f$bootstrap_p, 3),
    power_law_rejected = f$bootstrap_p < 0.1,
    vuong_stat = round(f$vuong_stat, 3), vuong_p = round(f$vuong_p, 3),
    lognormal_meanlog = round(f$meanlog, 3), lognormal_sdlog = round(f$sdlog, 3)
  )
}))

knitr::kable(
  m13_fit_summary,
  caption = "M1.3: MLE power-law fit (poweRlaw::conpl) and lognormal comparator (poweRlaw::conlnorm) at the same xmin, river and ocean pooled particle-length PSDs"
)
```

```{r m13-rq-propagation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Convert each model to an equivalent correction factor over the SAME measured
# window already used for the production correction factor
# (L_meas_min_use/L_meas_max_use), so only the extrapolation MODEL differs,
# not the physical measurement window -- then recompute the RQ for both ERMs
# against the already-computed production hazard (haz/haz_ocean; hazard is
# not re-derived here, only the exposure-side extrapolation model changes).
m13_propagate_one <- function(fit, L_meas_min, L_meas_max, monitoring_df, conc_col,
                               haz_df, n_risk, cpsd_a_psd, combined_cf_prod, seed_base) {

  cf_mle <- correction_factor(
    a = -fit$alpha_mle, L_meas_min = L_meas_min, L_meas_max = L_meas_max,
    L_tar_min = 1, L_tar_max = 5000, slope_convention = "differential"
  )
  # Computed from log upper-tail probabilities: when the tail above xmin is a
  # near-pure power law the lognormal MLE drifts to its power-law limit (very
  # negative meanlog, very large sdlog) and plain CDF differences underflow to 0/0.
  lS <- function(x) stats::plnorm(x, fit$meanlog, fit$sdlog, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
  cf_lognormal <- exp(lS(1) - lS(L_meas_min)) * (-expm1(lS(5000) - lS(1))) / (-expm1(lS(L_meas_max) - lS(L_meas_min)))
  stopifnot("lognormal CF is not finite" = is.finite(cf_lognormal) && cf_lognormal > 0)

  rq_for_cf <- function(cf_val, seed) {
    set.seed(seed)
    eed_i <- bootstrap_eed(monitoring_df[[conc_col]] * cf_val, n_boot = n_boot, probs = c(0.5, 0.95))
    set.seed(seed + 1)
    draws_i <- draw_rq_mc1d(haz_df, eed_i$q50, n_risk = n_risk) |>
      dplyr::filter(ERM %in% c("Food Dilution", "Tissue Translocation"), HCx == 5)
    draws_i |>
      dplyr::group_by(ERM) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        RQ_p50   = stats::median(RQ), P_exceed = mean(RQ > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
        RQ_p025  = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), RQ_p975 = stats::quantile(RQ, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups  = "drop"
      )
  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(
    rq_for_cf(median(combined_cf_prod), seed_base)     |> dplyr::mutate(Model = "Production (fixed-window MLE)", CF = median(combined_cf_prod)),
    rq_for_cf(cf_mle, seed_base + 10)                   |> dplyr::mutate(Model = "MLE power law", CF = cf_mle),
    rq_for_cf(cf_lognormal, seed_base + 20)              |> dplyr::mutate(Model = "Lognormal (tapered small-end)", CF = cf_lognormal)
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(Matrix = fit$matrix_label)
}

m13_river_rq <- m13_propagate_one(
  m13_river_fit, L_meas_min_use, L_meas_max_use, monitoring_pooled_scope, "C_measured_pL",
  haz_pooled, n_risk, cpsd_fit_all$a_psd, combined_cf_pooled, seed_base = 72001
)
m13_ocean_rq <- m13_propagate_one(
  m13_ocean_fit, L_meas_min_ocean, L_meas_max_ocean, monitoring_ocean, "C_measured_pL",
  haz_ocean, n_risk_ocean, cpsd_fit_ocean_all$a_psd, combined_cf_ocean, seed_base = 72002
)

m13_rq_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(m13_river_rq, m13_ocean_rq) |>
  dplyr::relocate(Matrix, Model, ERM, CF, RQ_p50, RQ_p025, RQ_p975, P_exceed)

knitr::kable(
  m13_rq_results, digits = 3,
  caption = "M1.3: Food Dilution and Tissue Translocation HC5 RQ under each extrapolation model, holding hazard fixed at the production values"
)
```

```{r m13-holdflip-vars, echo=FALSE}
# N3 Part B: the missing populated hold/flip conclusion. Every number pulled
# live from m13_rq_results / m13_fit_summary (already rendered above); no
# retyped literals, no conditional template left unpopulated.
m13_holdflip_one <- function(matrix_label) {
  rows <- m13_rq_results |> dplyr::filter(Matrix == matrix_label, ERM == "Food Dilution")
  cpsd <- rows |> dplyr::filter(Model == "Production (fixed-window MLE)")
  mle  <- rows |> dplyr::filter(Model == "MLE power law")
  logn <- rows |> dplyr::filter(Model == "Lognormal (tapered small-end)")
  if (nrow(cpsd) != 1 || nrow(mle) != 1 || nrow(logn) != 1) return(paste0("Model comparison rows were incomplete for ", matrix_label, " at this render."))
  status_word <- function(rq) if (rq > 1) "holds (RQ > 1)" else if (rq > 0.9) "is marginal (RQ near 1)" else "falls below 1"
  paste0(
    "For ", matrix_label, ", the production (fixed-window MLE) single-slope Food Dilution HC5 RQ is ", round(cpsd$RQ_p50, 3),
    " (P(RQ>1) = ", round(cpsd$P_exceed * 100, 1), "%); under the MLE power law it is ", round(mle$RQ_p50, 3),
    " (P(RQ>1) = ", round(mle$P_exceed * 100, 1), "%), so the exceedance ", status_word(mle$RQ_p50),
    "; under the lognormal small-end model it is ", round(logn$RQ_p50, 3), " (P(RQ>1) = ", round(logn$P_exceed * 100, 1),
    "%), so the exceedance ", status_word(logn$RQ_p50), "."
  )
}
m13_holdflip_river <- m13_holdflip_one("River water")
m13_holdflip_ocean <- m13_holdflip_one("Ocean water")

m13_xmin_river <- m13_fit_summary$xmin_um[m13_fit_summary$Matrix == "River water"]
m13_xmin_ocean <- m13_fit_summary$xmin_um[m13_fit_summary$Matrix == "Ocean water"]

m13_river_fd_logn <- m13_rq_results |> dplyr::filter(Matrix == "River water", ERM == "Food Dilution", Model == "Lognormal (tapered small-end)")
m13_ocean_fd_logn <- m13_rq_results |> dplyr::filter(Matrix == "Ocean water", ERM == "Food Dilution", Model == "Lognormal (tapered small-end)")
m13_bounding_word <- if (nrow(m13_river_fd_logn) == 1 && nrow(m13_ocean_fd_logn) == 1) {
  if (m13_river_fd_logn$RQ_p50 > 1 && m13_ocean_fd_logn$RQ_p50 > 1) {
    paste0(
      "Both matrices' Food Dilution RQ stays above 1 under the lognormal small-end model, so the exceedance is robust ",
      "to the extrapolation-model choice tested here -- this strengthens the \"cannot be excluded\" statement in the Key ",
      "Findings summary rather than qualifying it."
    )
  } else {
    paste0(
      "At least one matrix's Food Dilution RQ falls below 1 under the lognormal small-end model, so the exceedance is ",
      "not robust to this defensible small-end roll-off; read this alongside the sub-2.5 µm floor collapse (Section ",
      "12.5.1) and the piecewise river Food Dilution RQ (Section 13.3) as convergent evidence that the food-dilution ",
      "exceedance sits on the unconstrained sub-floor extrapolation zone."
    )
  }
} else "The lognormal-model comparison could not be completed for both matrices at this render budget."
```

**Guardrails and interpretation.** The fixed-window MLE single-slope fit is the production default; the xmin-based MLE power law and the lognormal are labelled comparators only, and hazard is never re-derived in this section (only the exposure-side extrapolation model changes, holding `haz`/`haz_ocean` fixed at their production values). Report GoF failures honestly: `r if (m13_fit_summary$power_law_rejected[m13_fit_summary$Matrix == "River water"]) "the power law IS rejected for river water (bootstrap p < 0.1)" else "the power law is NOT rejected for river water"`, and `r if (m13_fit_summary$power_law_rejected[m13_fit_summary$Matrix == "Ocean water"]) "IS rejected for ocean water" else "is NOT rejected for ocean water"` (bootstrap p = `r round(m13_fit_summary$bootstrap_p[m13_fit_summary$Matrix=="River water"],3)` river, `r round(m13_fit_summary$bootstrap_p[m13_fit_summary$Matrix=="Ocean water"],3)` ocean). The Vuong test indicates whether the power law and lognormal are statistically distinguishable at each matrix's shared `xmin` (p < 0.05 favors one model over the other; a non-significant result means the data cannot discriminate between them at this sample size; river Vuong statistic = `r round(m13_fit_summary$vuong_stat[m13_fit_summary$Matrix=="River water"],3)`, p = `r round(m13_fit_summary$vuong_p[m13_fit_summary$Matrix=="River water"],3)`; ocean statistic = `r round(m13_fit_summary$vuong_stat[m13_fit_summary$Matrix=="Ocean water"],3)`, p = `r round(m13_fit_summary$vuong_p[m13_fit_summary$Matrix=="Ocean water"],3)`).

**Hold/flip conclusion.** `r m13_holdflip_river` `r m13_holdflip_ocean` Both fits report `xmin` explicitly (`r round(m13_xmin_river,1)` µm river, `r round(m13_xmin_ocean,1)` µm ocean, Table M1.3-fits above); the fit constrains only the measured range at or above `xmin` -- the sub-`xmin` extrapolation to 1 µm remains model-dependent regardless of goodness-of-fit, the same unconstrained sub-floor zone the floor-sensitivity (Section 12.5.1) and piecewise (Section 13.3) analyses probe from other angles. `r m13_bounding_word` Because the power law is not rejected for either matrix (bootstrap p reported above), the lognormal is an admissible alternative, not a preferred one -- the honest statement is the RQ range across admissible models, weighted by the (non-)discriminating Vuong result. Mechanistically, food dilution is a large-particle (volume/gut-filling) mechanism while small particles preferentially drive translocation; admitting small-particle studies into the volume-based food-dilution SSD (Section 12.5.1.3.1) is the plausible reason a shifted extrapolation model would move the RQ -- this section tests the *effect* of the extrapolation model choice, not that specific mechanism, directly. Ocean fiber (5 populated C-PSD bins) remains excluded from MLE fitting as too sparse for a stable tail fit; the pooled-"all"-shapes basis is used for both matrices' MLE/lognormal fits.

## 12.5.3 River vs ocean polymer composition: test for buoyant-polymer enrichment

A shift in polymer mix at the sea surface — specifically enrichment of buoyant polymers (PP, PE) relative to rivers — would independently support a surface-retention/transport interpretation of the shallower ocean particle-length PSD slope (Section 12.1.1), rather than a source/residence or fitting-window explanation. `buoyancy_freshwater`/`buoyancy_marine` are already assigned per particle by `assign_polymer_density()` (Section 3.1.1), relative to freshwater (1.00 g/cm³) and seawater (1.025 g/cm³) respectively, so no new density-assignment code is needed here — only the statistical test.

```{r m14-polymer-composition, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# sample_depth_general is entirely NA for every ocean-water particle in this
# study (all 6 ocean sample IDs; confirmed below) -- these µFTIR runs simply
# did not record a depth stratum for ocean grabs, unlike river water, which
# has both strata. Ocean is therefore its own "depth not recorded" level
# rather than being assumed to be "surface" -- no depth label is fabricated
# for data that was not collected with one.
m14_particles <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  raw_particles_river |> dplyr::mutate(Matrix = "River water"),
  raw_particles_ocean |> dplyr::mutate(Matrix = "Ocean water")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Depth = dplyr::case_when(
      Matrix == "Ocean water" ~ "depth not recorded",
      TRUE ~ as.character(sample_depth_general)
    )
  )

m14_ocean_depth_recorded <- sum(!is.na(raw_particles_ocean$sample_depth_general))

m14_contingency <- table(m14_particles$polymer_density_group, m14_particles$Matrix)

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame.matrix(m14_contingency),
  caption = paste0(
    "River (n = ", sum(m14_particles$Matrix == "River water"), ") vs ocean (n = ",
    sum(m14_particles$Matrix == "Ocean water"), ") polymer-group contingency table."
  )
)

# Fisher's exact if any expected cell count is small (chi-square approximation
# becomes unreliable below ~5 expected per cell); chi-square otherwise.
m14_expected_min <- suppressWarnings(min(chisq.test(m14_contingency)$expected))
m14_full_test <- if (m14_expected_min < 5) {
  fisher.test(m14_contingency, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)
} else {
  chisq.test(m14_contingency)
}
cat(
  "Full polymer x matrix test:", m14_full_test$method,
  "-- statistic =", if (!is.null(m14_full_test$statistic)) signif(m14_full_test$statistic, 4) else NA,
  ", p =", signif(m14_full_test$p.value, 4),
  "(min expected cell count =", round(m14_expected_min, 2), ")\n"
)
```

```{r m14-buoyant-2x2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Focused 2x2 test: buoyant (PP + PE) vs non-buoyant, river vs ocean. PP and PE
# are the only two polymer groups classified "buoyant" under both
# buoyancy_freshwater and buoyancy_marine in this dataset (verified below),
# so "buoyant" here is defined directly by polymer identity rather than by
# picking one of the two medium-specific buoyancy columns.
m14_particles <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::mutate(is_buoyant = polymer_density_group %in% c("polyethylene", "polypropylene"))

m14_buoyancy_agreement <- mean(m14_particles$buoyancy_freshwater == m14_particles$buoyancy_marine)

m14_2x2 <- table(m14_particles$is_buoyant, m14_particles$Matrix)
m14_2x2_test <- if (min(suppressWarnings(chisq.test(m14_2x2)$expected)) < 5) {
  fisher.test(m14_2x2)
} else {
  chisq.test(m14_2x2, correct = TRUE)
}

m14_buoyant_fraction <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::group_by(Matrix) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    n_buoyant = sum(is_buoyant),
    fraction_buoyant = n_buoyant / n,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ci = list(stats::binom.test(n_buoyant, n)$conf.int),
    ci_low  = ci[1],
    ci_high = ci[2]
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(-ci)

knitr::kable(
  m14_buoyant_fraction, digits = 3,
  caption = "Buoyant-polymer (PP + PE) fraction by matrix, with binomial 95% CIs",
  col.names = c("Matrix", "n", "n buoyant", "Fraction buoyant", "95% CI low", "95% CI high")
)

cat(
  "Buoyant (PP+PE) vs non-buoyant x river/ocean:", m14_2x2_test$method,
  "-- p =", signif(m14_2x2_test$p.value, 4), "\n"
)
cat(
  "buoyancy_freshwater and buoyancy_marine agree for", scales::percent(m14_buoyancy_agreement, accuracy = 0.1),
  "of particles in this dataset -- i.e. essentially no polymer group in the current density lookup ",
  "(Hidalgo-Ruz et al. 2012) falls in the narrow density band (1.00-1.025 g/cm3) that would flip ",
  "classification between freshwater and seawater reference density.\n"
)

# By-group (Ocean / River-surface / River-subsurface) breakdown for the plot
# below, since ocean has no recorded depth stratum in this dataset (Section
# 12.5.3.1) -- it stays a single pooled group rather than being split.
m14_buoyant_fraction_bygroup <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Group = dplyr::case_when(
      Matrix == "Ocean water" ~ "Ocean water",
      Matrix == "River water" & Depth == "surface"    ~ "River - surface",
      Matrix == "River water" & Depth == "subsurface" ~ "River - subsurface",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Group)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), n_buoyant = sum(is_buoyant), fraction_buoyant = n_buoyant / n, .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(ci = list(stats::binom.test(n_buoyant, n)$conf.int), ci_low = ci[1], ci_high = ci[2]) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(-ci)

knitr::kable(
  m14_buoyant_fraction_bygroup, digits = 3,
  caption = "Buoyant-polymer (PP + PE) fraction by group (river split by depth stratum; ocean pooled, no recorded depth), with binomial 95% CIs",
  col.names = c("Group", "n", "n buoyant", "Fraction buoyant", "95% CI low", "95% CI high")
)

# River surface-vs-subsurface buoyancy test: same one-sided H1 (surface
# fraction > subsurface fraction) and the same expected-cell-count fallback
# convention as Section 12.5.3.1.1's dedicated treatment of this question,
# computed locally here too so this plot's annotation is self-contained
# rather than forward-referencing a later section.
m14_river_depth_2x2 <- table(
  factor(m14_particles$Depth[m14_particles$Matrix == "River water"], levels = c("subsurface", "surface")),
  m14_particles$is_buoyant[m14_particles$Matrix == "River water"]
)
m14_river_depth_expected_min <- suppressWarnings(min(chisq.test(m14_river_depth_2x2)$expected))
m14_river_depth_test <- if (m14_river_depth_expected_min < 5) {
  fisher.test(m14_river_depth_2x2, alternative = "greater")
} else {
  stats::prop.test(
    x = rev(m14_river_depth_2x2[, "TRUE"]), n = rev(rowSums(m14_river_depth_2x2)), alternative = "greater"
  )
}
cat(
  "River surface vs subsurface buoyant fraction (one-sided H1: surface > subsurface):", m14_river_depth_test$method,
  "-- p =", signif(m14_river_depth_test$p.value, 4), "(see Section 12.5.3.1.1 for the full treatment)\n"
)
```

```{r m14-composition-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
m14_composition_plot <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::count(Matrix, polymer_density_group) |>
  dplyr::group_by(Matrix) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fraction = n / sum(n)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = polymer_density_group, y = fraction, fill = Matrix)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +

  ggplot2::coord_flip() +

    x = NULL, y = "Fraction of particles",

  ) +

ggsave(m14_composition_plot, filename = "figures/m14_composition_plot.png", width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300)
m14_composition_plot

m14_group_levels <- c("Ocean water", "River - surface", "River - subsurface")
m14_group_pal <- c("Ocean water" = "#009E73", "River - surface" = "#0072B2", "River - subsurface" = "#56B4E9")

m14_2x2_label <- paste0(
  "River (pooled) vs ocean: ", m14_2x2_test$method, ", p = ", signif(m14_2x2_test$p.value, 3),
  "\nRiver surface vs subsurface: ", m14_river_depth_test$method, ", p = ", signif(m14_river_depth_test$p.value, 3)
)
m14_buoyant_ymax <- max(m14_buoyant_fraction_bygroup$ci_high, na.rm = TRUE)

m14_buoyant_plot <- m14_buoyant_fraction_bygroup |>
  dplyr::mutate(Group = factor(Group, levels = m14_group_levels)) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = Group, y = fraction_buoyant, color = Group)) +

  ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 2, y = m14_buoyant_ymax * 1.28, label = m14_2x2_label,
                    size = 3.2, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30", lineheight = 1.1) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = m14_group_pal, guide = "none") +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Buoyant (PP + PE) fraction, with binomial 95% CI",
    title = "Buoyant-polymer fraction: ocean vs river (by depth stratum)",
    subtitle = "Ocean has no recorded depth stratum in this dataset (Section 12.5.3.1) -- shown pooled, not assumed surface."
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4))

ggsave(m14_buoyant_plot, filename = "figures/m14_buoyant_plot.png", width = 8, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
m14_buoyant_plot
```

**Interpretation.** A significant enrichment of PP/PE in ocean surface water relative to river water (`r scales::percent(m14_buoyant_fraction$fraction_buoyant[m14_buoyant_fraction$Matrix == "Ocean water"], accuracy=0.1)` vs `r scales::percent(m14_buoyant_fraction$fraction_buoyant[m14_buoyant_fraction$Matrix == "River water"], accuracy=0.1)`, 2×2 test p = `r signif(m14_2x2_test$p.value, 3)`) would support the transport/retention reading of the river-vs-ocean slope difference; a null result points instead toward a source/residence or fitting-window explanation. **Caveats.** Composition is count-based over each matrix's own measured detection window (the same LOD/window caveats that apply to the slope fits themselves), and ocean n = `r sum(m14_particles$Matrix == "Ocean water")` limits statistical power relative to river n = `r sum(m14_particles$Matrix == "River water")`. This polymer-composition test is an independent line of evidence that does *not* depend on the fitting window — but the river-vs-ocean **slope** difference itself (Section 12.1.1) is separately confounded by different fitting windows (river `r round(cpsd_fit_all$lower_lod_used_um)`–`r round(cpsd_fit_all$upper_lod_um)` µm vs ocean `r round(cpsd_fit_ocean_all$lower_lod_used_um)`–`r round(cpsd_fit_ocean_all$upper_lod_um)` µm) and should be re-tested over a common overlapping window before that slope difference alone is attributed to source or transport.

### 12.5.3.1 Depth-stratified polymer composition (river surface/subsurface vs ocean)

River water has both `sample_depth_general` strata (`r sum(raw_particles_river$sample_depth_general == "surface", na.rm=TRUE)` surface, `r sum(raw_particles_river$sample_depth_general == "subsurface", na.rm=TRUE)` subsurface particles). Ocean water does not: `sample_depth_general` is unrecorded for all `r nrow(raw_particles_ocean)` ocean-water particles in this study (`r m14_ocean_depth_recorded` with a recorded stratum), so an ocean depth split is not possible from this dataset -- ocean is shown below as its own "depth not recorded" panel rather than assumed to be surface-only. The top-5 polymers by pooled river+ocean particle count set a common comparison basis across panels; every other polymer group is collapsed to "Other" so rare groups do not fragment the comparison.

```{r m14-depth-composition-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
m14_top5_polymers <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::count(polymer_density_group, sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 5) |>
  dplyr::pull(polymer_density_group)

m14_depth_panel_levels <- c("River water - surface", "River water - subsurface", "Ocean water - depth not recorded")

m14_depth_composition <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    polymer_top5 = ifelse(polymer_density_group %in% m14_top5_polymers,
                           as.character(polymer_density_group), "Other"),
    polymer_top5 = factor(polymer_top5, levels = c(m14_top5_polymers, "Other")),
    panel = factor(paste(Matrix, Depth, sep = " - "), levels = m14_depth_panel_levels)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(panel)) |>
  dplyr::count(panel, polymer_top5) |>
  dplyr::group_by(panel) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fraction = n / sum(n), n_panel = sum(n)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

m14_depth_composition_plot <- m14_depth_composition |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = polymer_top5, y = fraction, fill = polymer_top5)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.2) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 3,
                       labeller = ggplot2::as_labeller(function(x) paste0(x, "\n(n = ",
                         m14_depth_composition$n_panel[match(x, m14_depth_composition$panel)], ")"))) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Fraction of particles",
    title = "Top-5 polymer composition by matrix and sampling depth",
    subtitle = "Ocean has no recorded depth stratum in this dataset (see text) -- shown as a single panel, not assumed to be surface"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
    panel.border = ggplot2::element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggsave(m14_depth_composition_plot, filename = "figures/m14_depth_composition_plot.png", width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300)
m14_depth_composition_plot
```

**Interpretation.** Comparing the two river panels isolates a within-matrix depth effect (same sampling program, same µFTIR workflow, same LOD window); comparing either river panel to the ocean panel still mixes a matrix effect with the unrecorded-depth limitation above. `r scales::percent(m14_buoyant_fraction$fraction_buoyant[m14_buoyant_fraction$Matrix == "Ocean water"], accuracy=0.1)` buoyant fraction in ocean vs river's surface/subsurface split (Section 12.5.3 table) is the more decision-relevant comparison than the full multi-polymer breakdown shown here, which is a descriptive, hypothesis-generating cross-tabulation. The within-river surface-vs-subsurface buoyancy comparison it motivates is tested formally below.

#### 12.5.3.1.1 Formal test: are buoyant particles relatively more abundant at the river surface than subsurface?

Rationale: if buoyant (PP + PE) particles float toward and accumulate at the air-water interface, the river surface stratum should show a higher buoyant *fraction* than the subsurface stratum sampled at the same locations and times. This is a directional (one-sided) hypothesis, tested only within river water -- ocean has no recorded depth stratum (Section 12.5.3.1 above), so it cannot be included.

```{r m14-depth-buoyancy-test, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
river_depth_buoyant <- m14_particles |>
  dplyr::filter(Matrix == "River water", Depth %in% c("surface", "subsurface")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Depth = factor(Depth, levels = c("subsurface", "surface")))

river_depth_buoyant_fraction <- river_depth_buoyant |>
  dplyr::group_by(Depth) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), n_buoyant = sum(is_buoyant), fraction_buoyant = n_buoyant / n, .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ci = list(stats::binom.test(n_buoyant, n)$conf.int),
    ci_low  = ci[1],
    ci_high = ci[2]
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(-ci)

knitr::kable(
  river_depth_buoyant_fraction, digits = 3,
  caption = "River water only: buoyant-polymer (PP + PE) fraction by sampling depth, with binomial 95% CIs.",
  col.names = c("Depth", "n", "n buoyant", "Fraction buoyant", "95% CI low", "95% CI high")
)

n_surf    <- river_depth_buoyant_fraction$n[river_depth_buoyant_fraction$Depth == "surface"]
n_sub     <- river_depth_buoyant_fraction$n[river_depth_buoyant_fraction$Depth == "subsurface"]
nb_surf   <- river_depth_buoyant_fraction$n_buoyant[river_depth_buoyant_fraction$Depth == "surface"]
nb_sub    <- river_depth_buoyant_fraction$n_buoyant[river_depth_buoyant_fraction$Depth == "subsurface"]
river_depth_2x2 <- table(river_depth_buoyant$Depth, river_depth_buoyant$is_buoyant)
river_depth_expected_min <- suppressWarnings(min(chisq.test(river_depth_2x2)$expected))

# One-sided two-proportion test: H1 = surface buoyant fraction > subsurface
# buoyant fraction. Falls back to a one-sided Fisher's exact test if any
# expected cell count is small (same threshold convention as Section 12.5.3's
# river-vs-ocean 2x2 test). river_depth_2x2 rows are (subsurface, surface) and
# columns are (not buoyant, buoyant), so a higher surface buoyant fraction
# implies odds ratio = (FALSE_sub * TRUE_surf) / (TRUE_sub * FALSE_surf) > 1
# -- alternative = "greater" is the correct one-sided direction for both tests.
river_depth_buoyancy_test <- if (river_depth_expected_min < 5) {
  fisher.test(river_depth_2x2, alternative = "greater")
} else {
  stats::prop.test(x = c(nb_surf, nb_sub), n = c(n_surf, n_sub), alternative = "greater")
}

cat(
  "Surface vs subsurface buoyant fraction, river water only:", river_depth_buoyancy_test$method,
  "-- one-sided H1: surface fraction > subsurface fraction -- p =", signif(river_depth_buoyancy_test$p.value, 4),
  "(min expected cell count =", round(river_depth_expected_min, 2), ")\n"
)
```

**Interpretation.** The river surface stratum's buoyant fraction is `r scales::percent(river_depth_buoyant_fraction$fraction_buoyant[river_depth_buoyant_fraction$Depth == "surface"], accuracy=0.1)` (n = `r n_surf`) versus `r scales::percent(river_depth_buoyant_fraction$fraction_buoyant[river_depth_buoyant_fraction$Depth == "subsurface"], accuracy=0.1)` at the subsurface (n = `r n_sub`); the one-sided test above gives p = `r signif(river_depth_buoyancy_test$p.value, 3)`. `r if (river_depth_buoyancy_test$p.value < 0.05) { "This supports the hypothesis that buoyant particles are relatively enriched at the river surface, consistent with density-driven vertical sorting within the water column." } else if (nb_surf / n_surf < nb_sub / n_sub) { "This does not support the hypothesis -- the observed direction is the opposite of what surface buoyant-enrichment would predict: the subsurface fraction is numerically higher than the surface fraction, though the 95% CIs above overlap substantially. Density-driven vertical sorting by buoyancy is not evident in this river dataset; the depth difference, if real, is more likely driven by something other than polymer buoyancy (e.g., local hydrodynamics, sampling time, or shape-dependent settling of non-buoyant fibers)." } else { "This does not provide statistically significant support for surface enrichment of buoyant particles at the conventional 0.05 threshold, though the observed fractions point in the hypothesized direction; the effect (if real) is smaller than this dataset's river n can resolve." }` This is a within-matrix, same-program, same-workflow comparison (unlike the river-vs-ocean buoyancy test in Section 12.5.3, which is additionally confounded by the ocean depth-recording gap noted above), so a significant result here would be comparatively strong evidence for local vertical sorting by buoyancy specifically.


# 15. Key Findings Summary

```{r key-findings, echo=FALSE}
kf_row <- function(matrix_label, shape_label, fo) tibble::tibble(
  Matrix = matrix_label, Shape = shape_label,
  a_psd = fo$a_psd, se = fo$se_a_psd,
  window = sprintf("%.0f–%.0f", fo$lower_lod_um, fo$upper_lod_um),
  n_window = fo$n_window %||% NA_real_,
```
